About the role

The Communications and Signal Processing Group at Imperial College has two part-time openings in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) to design a new layer of communication infrastructure using high-altitude platform systems (HAPS) to provide communications services to ground users. The positions are funded by the ARIA EndAP programme: https://aria.org.uk/opportunity-spaces/adaptive-machines/enduring-atmospheric-platforms/funded-projects?tabId=ta3&cardId=ai-enabled-haps . The post-holders will join a diverse team with expertise in network AI and optimization, wireless communications and networks, aircraft design and deployment regulations to leverage the strengths of different HAPS platforms, determine the best fleet composition, and coordinate platform movements for energy efficiency, resilience, and adaptability to traffic demands of ground users.

To begin, we will study how multiple HAPS platforms should be strategically moved and positioned in three-dimensional airspace to provide the optimal service coverage and meet communication quality of service (QoS) requirements for ground users subject to navigating weather, energy, and regulatory constraints. A robust backhaul network will be designed to connect HAPS with each other, and with terrestrial and satellite networks, ensuring efficient network-wide connectivity and flexibility.
We aim to develop a reinforcement-learning framework for joint optimization of air-vehicle design, real-time control, and provisioning of communication services under changing weather, energy availability, and regulatory constraints. Our goal is to develop novel distributed RL algorithms for each HAPS will function as an autonomous, distributed RL agent, making independent but cooperative control decisions to optimize its position, resource allocation, and operational strategy in real time. 
This post will also participate in assessment of alternative power architectures and operational constraints to ensure consistent power availability for both individual HAPS units and entire fleets. We will develop robust fleet operational strategies to identify minimum viable fleet sizes and configurations under varying weather, deployment, and coverage requirements. Furthermore, to use the designed algorithm in practice, we will evaluate how physical constraints, such as payload size, weight, and power supply, and techno-economic tradeoffs affect the optimal HAPS system designs. We will adapt and validate the developed HAPS technologies across multiple fleet platforms.
The positions are an excellent opportunity for researcher with strong background in machine learning, wireless communications and communication networks. Strong analytic skills are expected.

What you would be doing

Research Duties include:

To plan and carry out research in accordance with the project aims and timeframes.
To propose and investigate new techniques, algorithms and architectures for network design, optimization and orchestration.
To verify and characterize system performance both analytically and in realistic simulated testbeds.
To collaborate and cooperate with other research staff both within and outside Imperial College working on related projects funded by the UK EPSRC.
To act as the representative for Imperial College in meetings, conference calls and conferences.
To present research at conferences, workshops, open days and meetings, and publish research results in journals.
To develop a sound understanding of ethical and health and safety regulations, and the responsibilities of themselves and their colleagues

What we are looking for

Education

Research Associate: Hold a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience
*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.

Research Assistant: PhD (or equivalent) candidates in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a closely related discipline.

Experience

Machine learning (ML) and/or optimization for communication systems
Development, implementation and verification of ML algorithms in code
Algorithm development and performance analysis of data-driven decision-making systems

Knowledge

Machine learning and optimization techniques
Key technologies in wireless communication systems
Networked and distributed systems

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Please note that job descriptions cannot be exhaustive, and the post-holder may be required to undertake other duties, which are broadly in line with the above key responsibilities.

For any specific queries regarding the post please contact Prof Kin K. Leung (kin.leung@imperial.ac.uk)

 Contract Type:  Fixed Term Contract to Aug 2029

 The SuMaCer (Sustainable Manufacturing of Functional Ceramics for Europe’s Net-Zero Industry Energy Devices) project is a new, successful project within the EU’s Horizon 2030. The project is a large consortium of five academic institutions and eight industry partners, all working together on developing the energy devices needed to power the transition to Net Zero, spanning batteries, fuel cells and electrolysers. We are recruiting a highly motivated researcher with a background in life cycle assessment and a strong interest or background in energy materials or devices, to join a successful team at the University of Birmingham.

 Main Duties and Responsibilities 

 In line with the principles of Net Zero Pollution, the primary aims of this role are to embed life cycle thinking across the project and to gather the data required for Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) calculations. You will engage directly with the researchers involved in designing and running new manufacturing processes; assess the safety and sustainability of the selected materials, following the EU’s Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) framework; assess the sustainability of the manufacturing and recycling processes involved; track the economic and circularity indicators of the prototype devices and advise your fellow researchers on how to improve the sustainability of their processes.

 You will inform the research partners of the data required for your life cycle inventory, proactively gather that data and perform calculations to determine environmental hotspots and key impacts. You will update the project partners on the credentials of their processes and suggest a range of possible improvements that they could realistically implement, through leading and participating in eco-design workshops. As many of the processes involved will be at low technology readiness level (TRL), you will be required to extend your LCA calculations to provide prospective assessments, using well defined future scenarios. You will also perform technoeconomic assessments (TEA), to identify cost estimates, as well as scan for risks and opportunities in the energy and hydrogen sectors.

 Skills and Knowledge 

 The position requires an individual with a high-level of analytical capability. Expertise in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage:

 life cycle assessment,

 life cycle social assessment,

 techno-economic modelling,

 materials flow analysis,

 energy device supply chain modelling,

 energy device manufacturing,

 or recycling processes.

 Qualifications and Experience 

 Candidates should have a PhD in an area related to any of the areas listed above, broadly conceived. The ideal candidate will be a skilled communicator able to effectively disseminate complex information for academic and policy audiences. They will also be able to coordinate their work with others to engage with relevant expertise across the project’s wider research networks.

 For further information please contact Jacqueline Edge, j.s.edge@bham.ac.uk

Research Associate in Equitable Energy Systems
 Apply
The role

This is an opportunity to work within the ambitious and impactful SHINE project, bringing together an international, transdisciplinary team to understand and improve the design of energy systems to have a positive impact on well-being and inclusion in The Gambia and Ghana. Working with academic institutions, internationally recognised organisations, and government ministries in Ghana, The Gambia, South Africa, Nepal and Brazil, the project will research and develop design methodologies and pilot energy interventions that seek to drive an inclusive energy transition.

What will you be doing?

The role holder will closely collaborate with the international partners to implement pilot energy systems in The Gambia and Ghana, which will include overseas fieldwork. The role holder will follow a mixed-method approach, collecting and examining predominantly qualitative data (including but not limited to interviews, focus groups, participatory mapping) from the pilot energy systems. In addition, they will be integral in designing and refining the holistic SHINE framework incorporating data from the pilot energy systems. They will work closely with the broader SHINE team to understand the implications of the data and develop methods to further understand the linkages between energy systems and well-being.

You should apply if

You will have a strong background in qualitative social science, ideally within the energy access sector, with the ability to conduct participatory methods as well as code, analyse and draw out key themes from interviews, focus groups, and transect walks that can be used to inform energy system design and future policy. You will also be able to analyse quantitative data, with the ability to use programmes like SPSS, MATLAB, REDCap and Microsoft Excel to draw out statistical measures. You should have experience working with international, transdisciplinary teams, so you must be able to communicate clearly, effectively, and respectfully across cultures, languages and disciplines. You will need to support the project administration, including developing ethical applications and ensuring that the project adheres to relevant University of Bristol requirements for research studies as well as necessary reporting. You will likely need to travel as part of this post, with visits to the partners in The Gambia and Ghana to collaborate on the pilot studies. Previous international travel experience is advantageous.

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 3 November 2026

 

The Role

 

Project SUITE introduces disruptive, vehicle integrated innovations that unlock strategic benefits for customers and the broader energy system, matching the Innovation stream of Innovate UK’s DRIVE35 programme. Through cross sector collaboration with UK experts from industry and academia, project SUITE will explore the design and development of Integrated Energy Technologies for Zero Emission Vehicles.

 

Newcastle University will build on Nissan's vehicle-to-grid (V2G) machine learning model, to accurately forecast EV flexible capacity, allowing for system level innovation by incorporating EVs as essential balancing assets into the UK energy grid. The post holder will lead the technical contributions to the tasks associated with this activity as well as assisting with the management and coordination of Newcastle’s wider involvement in project SUITE.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf.  These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

We advocate for the transparent, appropriate, and inclusive use of metrics, guided by expert judgment, to support high-quality, impactful research that is open, collaborative and sustainable. Full time Salary Range: £35,608.00 - £46,049.00 per annum

 

About You

The Warwick Institute for Employment Research (IER) is seeking to appoint a Research Fellow to strengthen its employment and labour markets research. We are looking for a labour economist or other social scientist possessing high level quantitative skills who wants to undertake rigorous research addressing important labour market and related public policy questions.

 

You will have or be close to completing a PhD in labour economics or a relevant social science discipline and have a clear research focus on employment or labour markets. You will have strong applied quantitative research skills, including econometric and statistical methods, and experience of analysing labour market data. We would particularly welcome experience of using large-scale survey, administrative or linked datasets and applying appropriate methods to questions of policy relevance.

 

You should be able to demonstrate a developing programme of substantive employment/labour market research rather than methodological expertise alone. This research should align with IER’s existing programmes of work, see https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/ier/researchthemesoverview/

 

You will have the ability to produce rigorous academic research and communicate findings clearly to policymakers, practitioners and other non-academic audiences.

 

IER is multidisciplinary, and you should be comfortable collaborating with researchers from different disciplinary and methodological backgrounds while also being able to undertake independent research. You should have the ability to work across several research activities and work effectively with external research and policy partners.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About the Role

You will contribute to the design and delivery of externally funded research, undertake analysis using large-scale survey, administrative and/or linked data, and produce high-quality academic and policy facing outputs. You will work with colleagues across IER and the wider University and with external partners including government departments, public bodies and other research organisations.

 

We are particularly interested in candidates whose expertise complements and strengthens IER's work in areas such as skills and training, labour market transitions, labour supply and demand, wages, health and job quality, and the evaluation of employment and labour market policies.

 

The role provides an opportunity to develop your own area of research expertise while contributing to IER's wider programme of policy relevant employment and labour market research. Pending successful probation, this post is tenure track.

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£34,610 per annum).

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£35,608 per annum).

About the Department

IER is a research-only institute within the University of Warwick's Faculty of Social Sciences specialising in employment and labour market research. Its work combines academic research with a strong commitment to addressing contemporary public policy questions.

 

IER is strong on research income generation and impact. It undertakes major programmes of research for UK and international research funders, government departments, public bodies, charities and foundations. It has a very successful record of securing research funding. Its researchers work extensively with policymakers and practitioners and collaborate across disciplines within Warwick and with research partners in the UK and internationally. For nearly 50 years, IER has contributed to the development of labour market research and to the evidence used by governments and other organisations in designing employment and labour market policies and practices. The Institute combines rigorous academic research with commissioned and applied research and offers an environment in which researchers can develop both scholarly expertise and substantial policy engagement.

 

IER is externally accredited for the quality of its research services and is committed to maintaining an inclusive and collaborative research culture. It holds an Athena Swan Bronze award. In REF 2021 IER was submitted as part of Unit of Assessment 17 (Business & Management) and helped Warwick achieve a top 10 outcome nationally in this Unit.

 

For more information please see our website - https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/ier/

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by 11.59pm on the closing date. 

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

For informal queries, please contact Professor Chris Warhurst, IER Director at c.warhurst@warwick.ac.uk or Professor Trine Larsen at Trine.Larsen@warwick.ac.uk

 

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 Job Summary 

 This is a fixed-term Research Fellow position funded through HERMES (Hazardous Energy Recycling: Methods for Emerging Specialist Chemistries), a 30-month Innovate UK-funded project led by Recyclus Group Ltd in partnership with the University of Birmingham.

 Lithium-metal batteries (LMBs) are widely used across offshore energy, defence, healthcare, and IoT applications but currently have no viable commercial recycling route in the UK — unlike lithium-ion batteries, LMBs remain chemically reactive at end-of-life and pose serious fire, explosion, and emission risks under conventional shredding. This has driven large UK stockpiles and continued reliance on overseas disposal. HERMES will develop and validate a safe shredding and materials-recovery process for LMBs, building on Recyclus' existing commercial lithium-ion recycling capability.

 You will join the Energy Materials Group (EMG) in the School of Metallurgy and Materials to identify and validate optimum passivation, discharge, shredding, and materials-separation methods for reactive LMB chemistries, working within your area of specialism and contributing to bid-writing and funding generation as the project develops. This work will directly inform industrial shredder redesign and scale-up, contributing to a first-of-a-kind UK LMB processing capability.

 Main Responsibilities 

 Design and carry out experimental work to identify and characterise safe discharge and passivation methods for reactive lithium-metal battery chemistries.

 Investigate shredding parameters and processing atmospheres suitable for safely handling LMB cells.

 Develop and evaluate materials separation and recovery methods for shredded battery output streams, assessing recovery efficiency and purity.

 Generate data to inform industrial partner shredder redesign and process scale-up, working closely with their engineering team.

 Conduct safety and hazard assessments of materials and processes.

 Contribute technical input to life-cycle assessment of shredding/passivation routes.

 Prepare technical reports, publications, and conference outputs arising from the research.

 Support supervision of postdoctoral and technician staff and contribute to day-to-day laboratory coordination.

 Person Specification 

 Hold a Bachelor's degree in a Science or Engineering discipline relevant to the project, or equivalent qualifications.

 Hold, or be close to completion of, a PhD in an area relevant to materials recycling, battery manufacture, minerals or process engineering, chemistry, or mechanical, electronic or chemical engineering.

 Prior knowledge, experience and achievements in mechanical shredding or comminution processes, particle/material separation techniques, battery safety or reactive/hazardous chemistry handling, and analytical characterisation (e.g. ICP-OES, SEM, XRD, or XRF) is highly desirable; however, training will be given to the right candidate in these areas.

 Demonstrably high level of analytical capability; ability to communicate complex information clearly to a diverse audience; ability to work in an interdisciplinary team; ability to coordinate own work with others to avoid conflict or duplication of effort.

 Proven ability to assess resource requirements and use resources effectively.

 Informal enquiries can be made to Rob Sommerville ( r.sommerville@bham.ac.uk ).

Research Assistant / Associate in Operations Research

Job id: 160045. Salary: £39,076 - £52,514 per annum, including London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 12 October 2026. Closing date: 25 October 2026.

Business unit: Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sci. Department: Engineering.

Contact details: Rym M’Hallah. Rym.mhallah@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Strand Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us

Recently re-founded, the Department of Engineering is rapidly expanding into a world-class research and teaching department. Research currently focuses on robotics, telecommunications and biomedical engineering, but we are looking to establish new research themes.

We offer both undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, with a distinctive approach, combining both traditional teaching methods with modern, project-based learning, catering for the needs of our students and the industries in which they will work.

As a new department we have invested in new laboratories and maker space at the centre of the Strand campus in the heart of central London.

For more information:  https://www.kcl.ac.uk/engineering

The position is funded by an EPSRC research grant whose vision is to offer an attractive, flexible, low-carbon, scaled, sustainable Demand Responsive Transport by offering optimised, scaled routing and scheduling and integrating dynamic pricing with behavioural insights.

About the role

We are advertising for a Research Assistant or Research Associate position at King’s College London to work with Prof. Rym M’Hallah (King’s), Prof. Christine Currie (University of Southampton), Prof. Julia Bennell, and Dr. Chiara Calastri (University of Leeds) on large scale optimization techniques and revenue management with applications to Demand responsive transport systems.

The researcher will undertake research specifically developing routing and scheduling methodologies. Of particular interest is the development and investigation of exact and heuristic optimisation approaches for routing and scheduling using stochastic data. The researcher will be expected to engage in problem formulation, algorithm implementation (using appropriate solver software and programming languages), experimental design and analysis of results. In addition, the research includes embedding pricing methodologies (already developed) and behavioural insights (provided through another work package).

The successful candidate will be part of a research team with five other members. You will be expected to engage in regular online and in person meetings, develop presentations for academic and practitioner audiences, and write reports and journal articles.

The successful candidate should have a PhD (or have submitted a thesis and awaiting results) in Operations Research, Mathematics, Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, or Transport Engineering and be proficient in a mainstream programming language. Candidates with a Masters degree in relevant subject areas will be considered for a Research Assistant role.

The post will be based within the Department of Engineering, located at the Strand campus of King's, in the centre of London. The post involves routine working on campus at King’s and regular in-person meetings at Leeds and Southampton.

This is a full-time post - 100% full time equivalent. It will be offered on a fixed-term contract until 31st May 2027.

For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Professor, Rym M’Hallah.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

1.       For grade six Research Associate role - PhD qualified in relevant subject area (or pending results): Operations Research, Mathematics, Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Transport Engineering. For grade five Research Assistant role - Masters degree in relevant subject area 

2.       Strong foundation in mathematics and deep knowledge of exact optimization techniques, heuristics and matheuristics   

3.       Experience of using and implementing mathematical programming (including constraint programming)  

4.       Proven track record of high-quality research publications in peer reviewed journals and international conferences  

5.       Excellent programming skills (including Python and off-the-shelf solvers)  

6.       Experience in using and implementing stochastic optimization and simulation  

7.       Excellent written and oral communication skills  

8.       Ability to work co-operatively within a team striving for collective excellence. 

Desirable criteria

1.       Good understanding of the concepts of revenue management 

2.       Understanding of Behavioural Science   

Knowledge of digital twin systems  

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the next page after you click “Apply Now”. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs or in their second year of their PhD will be considered if they have competitive CVs. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6. 

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university. 

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

To find out how our managers will review your application, please take a look at our ‘How we Recruit’ pages.

Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today.

We are now looking for highly motivated Research Fellow (PDRA) to develop and conduct individual and/or collaborative research projects. This is a 24-month fixed-term appointment supported by the EPSRC-funded Maritime and Last Mile Net Zero (MaLaMi) Place Based Impact Acceleration Account, under the supervision of Professor Zaili Yang, offering an opportunity to contribute to innovative research and practical solutions for maritime and last-mile decarbonisation.

You will support the development and application of quantitative and data-driven approaches to address challenges in maritime transportation, sustainable logistics and decarbonisation, with particular focus on Engineering Net Zero, Artificial Intelligence (AI), digitalisation and data. The work will contribute to evidence-based decision-making, the development of practical solutions and the advancement of sustainable transport systems.

Key responsibilities include: 1) contributing to scoping, feasibility assessment and proof-of-concept development for maritime and last-mile decarbonisation projects; 2) supporting the development and application of quantitative and data-driven models, including modelling, simulation, optimisation and machine learning; and 3) assisting in the development, testing and evaluation of analytical tools, prototypes and demonstrators, working collaboratively with academic researchers and external partners.

You should possess a good honours degree and a PhD (or equivalent professional experience) in transport, logistics, engineering, operations research, data science or a relevant discipline. You must demonstrate strong quantitative research and data-analysis capabilities, proficiency in programming or analytical tools, and the ability to disseminate research findings through high-quality publications in international journals and refereed conferences. Experience with research or innovation projects related to maritime decarbonisation, sustainable logistics, AI, digitalisation or proof-of-concept development is preferred.

You will work as part of the EPSRC-funded MaLaMi programme, collaborating with an interdisciplinary team of researchers, investigators and external partners, within the Liverpool Logistics Offshore and Marine Research Institute (LOOM) at Liverpool John Moores University, UK. LOOM enjoys an international research reputation in maritime risk studies, https://www.ljmu.ac.uk/research/centres-and-institutes/loom.

In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies.

This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do.

If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you.

The School/department is committed to promoting equality and diversity, including the Athena SWAN Gender Equality charter for promoting the career of women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) in higher education. We particularly welcome applications from women for this post and all appointments will be made on merit.

Please note all of our vacancies will be closed to applications at midnight on the advertised closing date, unless otherwise stated.

 University of Salford 

 - Research and Knowledge Exchange

 This is an exciting opportunity for an ambitious Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning graduate to fast-track their career development as a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) Associate. The successful candidate will undertake a 36-month collaborative project between R&B Switchgear Services Ltd and the University of Salford. R&B Switchgear is a UK manufacturer and service provider specialising in low-voltage switchgear and power distribution systems, serving sectors including healthcare, marine, renewables, utilities and data centres.

 The Knowledge Transfer Partnership scheme is one of the UK's largest graduate recruitment schemes ( http://ktp.innovateuk.org/ ) and is a three-way collaborative project between the Associate, the company and the knowledge base. It provides an opportunity for the successful applicant to manage a challenging project central to the company’s strategic development and long-term growth.

 This opportunity may close early depending on application volumes. 

 What will you be doing?
 This project presents a significant technical challenge, offering substantial opportunities for technical, commercial, leadership and professional development.

 You will be responsible for developing and embedding advanced artificial intelligence technologies capable of analysing complex engineering information across visual and text-based sources. This will involve combining computer vision, natural language processing and large language models to streamline time-intensive engineering and operational activities.

 A key challenge will be developing safe AI systems capable of operating within safety-critical engineering environments. You will work with complex multimodal datasets, train and evaluate machine learning models and ensure AI outputs are accurate, transparent and trusted by engineering teams.

 You will manage a strategically important innovation project and work closely with engineering, operational, IT and leadership teams. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills will be essential, as you will be required to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences and support the adoption of AI technologies across the business.

 Who are we looking for? 

 A graduate with a minimum 2.1 BEng/BSc in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Machine Learning or a related subject.

 Knowledge and demonstrable experience applying machine learning techniques to real-world problems.

 Experience in computer vision, natural language processing and large language models.

 Experience of developing, testing and deploying machine learning models.

 Understanding of data engineering, software development and AI deployment practices.

 Experience of Safe AI, cybersecurity or regulated environments would be advantageous.

 Additional added benefits
 To facilitate professional development, the successful candidate will receive extensive practical and formal training, gain highly desirable specialist business skills, broaden knowledge and expertise within an industrially relevant project, and gain valuable experience from their industry and academic mentors. The KTP Associate will also benefit from a Personal Development Budget of £6,000 (over and above their salary).

 As part of the wider R&B Switchgear Group, the Associate will also have access to a comprehensive employee benefits package designed to support wellbeing, work-life balance and long-term development. This includes an optional 9-day fortnight, providing a four-day week every other week, annual pay reviews and bonus opportunities, a one-week Christmas shutdown, company pension scheme, family-friendly policies, occupational health and GP support, an employee referral scheme, paid sick leave, paid paternity leave and wellbeing support.

 Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK

 Full time starting salary is normally in the range £30,062 to £31,900, with potential progression once in post to £35,883

 Fixed Term Contract to 31/10/2028

 Job Summary 

 The University of Birmingham is a partner in HERMES (Hazardous Energy Recycling: Methods for Emerging Specialist Chemistries), a project funded by Innovate UK and led by Recyclus Group Ltd, developing a safe shredding and materials-recovery process for lithium-metal batteries (LMBs).

 LMBs are used widely across offshore energy, defence, healthcare and IoT applications, but have no viable commercial recycling route in the UK. Unlike lithium-ion batteries, they remain chemically reactive at end-of-life and present fire, explosion and emission risks under conventional processing, leaving large unprocessed UK stockpiles. HERMES will establish optimum passivation, discharge, shredding and materials-separation methods for reactive LMB chemistries.

 You will support the day-to-day operation of the HERMES project within the Energy Materials Group in the School of Metallurgy and Materials. You will be carrying out technical laboratory work in the safe handling and recycling of batteries. The role involves close collaboration with academics, technical staff, students and the project's industrial partner.

 Main Responsibilities 

 Safe handling, discharge, disassembly and passivation of reactive lithium-metal cells and batteries prior to mechanical processing.

 Supporting the operation of laboratory-scale shredding and comminution equipment, including work under inert (nitrogen) atmospheres and within safety chambers.

 Mechanical separation and sorting of shredded battery output streams, including sieving, density and magnetic separation techniques.

 Preparation and characterisation of recovered materials and shredding aids, using techniques such as SEM, XRD, XRF and ICP-OES.

 Collection, entry and management of experimental data, and maintenance of laboratory records.

 Supporting gas and emissions sampling and monitoring during processing trials.

 Providing technical support to the battery recycling and energy materials laboratories, including maintenance of equipment, consumables and laboratory housekeeping.

 Ensuring compliance with health and safety requirements, including risk assessments and COSHH.

 Person Specification 

 Extensive relevant practical experience in a technical role, or a relevant degree/qualification with appropriate experience.

 GCSE Maths and English at grade C/4 or above, or equivalent.

 Demonstrable knowledge, experience, and understanding of laboratory health and safety is essential, including working with fume cupboards, inert gas supplies, and pressurised gas bottles and regulators.

 Working knowledge of batteries and battery safety is desirable, though relevant training will be given to the successful candidate.

 Practical experience of mechanical materials processing (e.g. shredding, milling, comminution) or materials separation techniques is desirable.

 Experience of analytical characterisation techniques (e.g. SEM, XRD, XRF, ICP-OES) is desirable.

 Strong communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to promote health and safety compliance in a laboratory environment.

 Informal enquiries to Dr Rob Sommerville, R.Sommerville@bham.ac.uk

 Knowledge Transfer Partnerships (KTPs) are a unique UK-wide activity that help businesses to improve their competitiveness and productivity by making better use of the knowledge, technology and skills within universities, colleges and research organisations.

 THE PROJECT
 The University of Essex in partnership with Sports Information Services Ltd offers an exciting opportunity to a graduate with the relevant skills and knowledge to develop novel computer vision-based techniques for information capture and analysis of live-broadcasted eSports events.

 DUTIES OF THE POST
 The duties of the post will include:

 The design and delivery of a bespoke capability to process live streams of games and gamers to identify in-game events to support the collection of data and associated statistics.

 Align live-captured data to improve the quality of prices (odds) for both in-play markets and future pre-match markets for future events.

 To implement the capability for extremely low-latency AI calculations, able to react to the accumulation of statistics across the course of a game.

 To make use of historical game data and video feeds to identify irregular play patterns.

 Communicating the objectives and progress of a project effectively with key internal stakeholders.

 Combining the usage of multiple coding languages by delivering a final product using the appropriate technology, such as Python, whilst working alongside colleagues familiar with Java and .NET.

 To contribute to the development of in-house AI and data science capabilities within SIS TV in order to increase operational independence.

 These duties are a guide to the work that the post holder will initially be required to undertake. They may be changed from time to time to meet changing circumstances. 

 KEY REQUIREMENTS
 Qualifications 

 MSc in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science or another STEM degree (essential).

 Skills and Experience 

 Thorough understanding of machine learning and deep neural networks; experience of designing and deploying machine learning-enabled tools.

 An understanding of fundamentals of Computer Vision and Video processing as a discipline of AI.

 Experience of building algorithms to process mixed structured / unstructured data.

 Experience of coding in Python, with good command of Tensorflow or Pytorch and related libraries.

 Experience in developing, training and evaluating predictive models using machine learning or deep learning methods.

 Strong general programming skills, with a proficiency in the use of Java.

 Attributes 

 A keen desire to learn new concepts.

 Demonstrable leadership potential.

 An ability to work independently, to use initiative and work as part of team.

 Strong problem-solving skills, with a particular emphasis on creative solutions.

 Good project management skills.

 An ability to write technical documentation and communicate complex technical issues to a non-technical audience effectively.

 An ability to process video data using computer vision techniques including object detection, pose estimation and temporal analysis.

 An ability to design predictive modelling approaches.

 Previous experience working in an industry setting (desirable).

 LOCATION

postings.title: Janeway Institute Postdoctoral Research Fellowship (Research Assistant or Research Associate) (Fixed Term)
postings.listing_context: Janeway Institute Postdoctoral Research Fellowship (Research Assistant or Research Associate) (Fixed Term) Faculty of Economics £34,610-£35, 608 £37,694-£46,049 Research 27 August 2026 15 December 2026 JH50885
postings.advert_text:
Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 3 years in the first instance.

The Janeway Institute at the Faculty of Economics, Cambridge University has a Postdoctoral Research Fellowship available for candidates working on areas of economics related to transmission mechanisms and economic policy. Eligible candidates include those who have recently been awarded a doctoral degree or expect to receive their degree by September 2027.

The Fellowship is for a maximum period of three years, but candidates can request a shorter term of one to two academic year(s) if this is a better fit for their career plans. The Fellowships will be based at the Janeway Institute. The Janeway Institute was created to develop new fundamental ideas, methods and research which push the frontier of economics. Fellows also have the possibility of joining a Cambridge College.

We welcome applications from researchers working on areas of economics related to transmission mechanisms and economic policy. This includes but is not limited to research into the contributions of firms and sectors in the aggregate economy; inquiries into how heterogeneity across households and firms shapes economic outcomes and contributes to economic growth; studies of the conduct and impact of monetary and fiscal policy in closed and open economies; and investigations of other economic factors that shape the economy and contribute to economic growth.

For more information see https://www.janeway.econ.cam.ac.uk/

Successful candidates should demonstrate an ability to develop their own research ideas and indicate how they can contribute to the transmission mechanisms research group in Cambridge. It is expected that successful candidates' work will be at the cutting edge of the research frontier with a view to future publications in world leading journals.

Successful candidates who have not yet received their PhD by September 2027 will be appointed on University Grade 5 as Research Assistants, starting at Grade 5, spine point 38 (£34,610 per annum). Upon award of the PhD, their salary will be upgraded to Grade 7 as Research Associates (Fellowships), starting at Grade 7, spine point 41 (£37,694 per annum) in the first year. In the second year, the salary will rise to spine point 42 (£38,784), and in the third year to spine point 43 (£39,906).

Janeway Teaching Fellowships, which provide supplemental remuneration on top of the Research Fellowship salary listed above, are available for those interested in gaining valuable teaching experience and contributing to the learning environment. These opportunities are contingent on the Faculty's needs and the candidate being suitably qualified. Further details, including the amount of additional remuneration, can be discussed during the interview process.

Applications should consist of:

A curriculum vitae; expression of interest cover letter outlining how you would be able to contribute to the Janeway Institute in light of your research interests; a job market paper; supplementary material such as other available research papers.

Three references will be sought upon receipt of application.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Queries may be directed to Marion Reusch, Janeway Institute Administrator, ji@econ.cam.ac.uk

Please quote reference JH50885 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

postings.advert_text:
Research Associate in AI

Job id: 160725. Salary: £45,031- 47,379 Including London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 20 October 2026. Closing date: 10 November 2026.

Business unit: Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine. Department: Department of Infectious Diseases.

Contact details: Professor Tania Dottorini. tania.dottorini@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: No category added.

Back to job search

About the role

King’s College London is a world leading research-intensive university with a strong international profile and a long-standing commitment to addressing major societal and global challenges.

This role is based within the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine, in the School of Immunology & Microbial Science in the Department of Infectious Diseases. It brings together expertise across microbiology, immunology, clinical sciences, data science and artificial intelligence.

The Department offers a highly interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, with strong links to clinical partners and access to outstanding research infrastructure and cross faculty initiatives.

About us

This is an exciting project Supported by the BBSRC. Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is one of the biggest public health challenges of our time. In 2019, 1.27 million deaths were attributed to antibiotic resistant bacteria. The gut microbiome is composed of harmless symbionts, commensal bacteria, and opportunistic pathogens, all of which play crucial roles in human and animal health and disease. In physiological conditions the gut microbiome is stable, but when perturbative events occur (e.g., dietary changes, infections, stress, antibiotic administration) the population of microbiota changes, influencing health and protection against further colonisation. These changes may involve new resistant bacteria becoming permanent residents or transferring resistance to the commensals). The core concepts underlying our project are: to gaining a better understanding of how the gut microbiome changes as consequence of infection, co-infection, or treatment (including the development of resistant traits) is a fundamental starting point towards understanding the mechanisms of inception and spread of endemic diseases and antimicrobial resistance.

The research associate will be responsible for developing, implementing and applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning and data-mining methods to address complex research questions. They will lead the analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, including sequencing, sensor, biological and medical data, and ensure robust, reproducible computational workflows.

The postholder will be responsible for developing and applying AI methods across the following areas, demonstrated through scientific publications or other academic/industrial achievements:

Generative AI (text and numerical data; excluding image, audio, video generation)
Agentic AI, orchestration, and adaptive systems (continuous feedback, dynamic reasoning, self-optimisation)
AI methods for mining, classifying, and forecasting from heterogeneous data sources
Spatial-temporal statistics/modelling from heterogeneous data (Bayesian hierarchical models, autoregressive models, random fields)
Sequence/time-series modelling and language models, particularly transformer architectures
Explainable AI methods
Causal AI methods
Machine learning

This is a full-time post 35 Hours a week, and you will be offered a fixed term contract until 31st August 2028. 

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information. 

About you 

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

PhD (or close to completion) in Computer Science, AI, Statistics, or a closely related field
Machine learning and deep learning
Generative AI (text and numbers; excluding image, audio, video generation)
Agentic AI, orchestration, and adaptive systems (continuous feedback, dynamic reasoning, self-optimisation)
AI methods for mining, classifying, and forecasting from heterogeneous data sources
Spatial-temporal statistics/modelling from heterogeneous data (Bayesian hierarchical models, autoregressive models, random fields
Sequence/time-series modelling and language models, particularly transformer architectures
Explainable AI methods

Desirable criteria

Experience with data analysis in the context of infectious diseases, epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance
Experience in the development of diagnostics and /or therapeutics solutions, drug-discovery

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university.

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

To find out how our managers will review your application, please take a look at our ‘How we Recruit’ pages.

Interviews are due to be held on 23/10/2026

Job Title:  Research Assistant in Machine Learning for Epidemiology
Posting Start Date:  13/10/2026
Job Id:  3178
School/Department:  Computer Science

Contract Type:  Fixed-term
Salary per annum (£):  £32,080 pro rata
Closing Date:  08/11/2026

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

Strep A is a common bacterial infection that causes spectacular, unexpected outbreaks of disease every few years. The cause of these outbreaks is unknown, but several factors are likely to contribute, for example, the burden of circulating viral infections. This project strives to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven early warning system to predict the risk of Strep A outbreaks and upsurges before they occur. The RA will work to integrate multiple datasets and apply a combination of mathematical modelling methods, including time-series modelling and probabilistic machine learning. Anticipated work includes developing and training models, with validation and refinement steps using retrospective data and simulation work undertaken where appropriate. This will be followed by a further evaluation phase to assess model performance, usability, and potential for real-world application using prospective data.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

Collate, clean and prepare epidemiological datasets from a range of sources, ensuring data quality.
Apply and help develop machine learning models, including feature preparation, model selection, fitting, and hyperparameter tuning.
Conduct exploratory data analysis and produce descriptive statistics and clear visualisations.
Contribute to model evaluation and validation, including selecting appropriate performance metrics demonstrating model generalisability to the real world.
Ensure all activities comply with data protection legislation, research ethics requirements, and information governance procedures for handling sensitive health data.
Work proactively and on own initiative, responding constructively to feedback from the line managers / principal investigators.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Experience in cleaning, wrangling, and preparing structured datasets for analysis

Company: University of Warwick

Job Title: Research Fellow

Reference:  463             

Department: Physics

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 30 September 2029

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date:  Thursday 10 December 2026, 11:59pm (UK)                       

Full time Salary Range: £36,320.00 - £46,970.00 per annum

About the Role

The Semiconductor Research Group (https://warwick.ac.uk/silicon) in the Department of Physics at the University of Warwick is recruiting a Research Fellow with outstanding experimental skills in semiconductor materials science and cryogenic electrical characterisation.

 

The appointment supports a collaborative EPSRC–NSF project with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), USA: “Towards Ultralow-Noise SiGe Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors for Quantum Technology and Beyond: Epitaxial Engineering of Cryogenic Charge Transport.”

 

The research investigates how epitaxial layer design, alloy composition, strain, doping, interfaces and defects govern the electrical characteristics of SiGe heterojunctions and ultimately the cryogenic performance of SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs).

 

You will investigate Si/SiGe heterostructures grown using Warwick’s in-house reduced-pressure chemical vapour deposition (RP-CVD) facilities.

 

A defining element of the role is independently performing and interpreting current–voltage (I–V), capacitance–voltage (C–V) and conductance–voltage (G–V) measurements over temperatures from room temperature down to approximately 2 K. This includes assessment of bias-, frequency- and temperature-dependent effects, experimental artefacts, and the physical mechanisms responsible for non-ideal junction behaviour.

 

You will integrate these results with rigorous structural and materials characterisation, particularly cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (XTEM/TEM), high-resolution X-ray diffraction (HR-XRD), atomic force microscopy (AFM) and relevant complementary methods.

 

Your findings will inform the interpretation and optimisation of SiGe epitaxial heterostructures and provide the materials perspective for the international project team.

 

HBT device fabrication is undertaken by collaborators, not at Warwick. Where relevant, the role may include focused ion beam (FIB) specimen preparation and SEM/XTEM characterisation of collaborator-fabricated HBTs.

 

You will benefit from specialist semiconductor and low-temperature measurement facilities, scientific collaboration with Caltech and opportunities to publish and present internationally.

 

This is a laboratory-based experimental research position requiring full-time on-site working at the University of Warwick. The successful candidate will be expected to work in person within the Semiconductor Research Group's laboratories and research facilities. Due to the hands-on nature of the experimental activities, including specialist semiconductor materials characterisation and cryogenic electrical measurements, remote or hybrid working arrangements are not available for this position.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are seeking an accomplished, experimentally focused semiconductor materials scientist with a PhD, or near completion of a PhD, in semiconductor physics, materials science, materials engineering or a related discipline.

 

You will bring a convincing record of high-quality original experimental work, sound scientific judgement and clear personal contributions to research outputs.

 

An essential requirement is substantial, direct hands-on experience of all three semiconductor electrical techniques: current–voltage (I–V), capacitance–voltage (C–V) and conductance–voltage (G–V).

 

You must also demonstrate practical low-temperature electrical measurement experience from room temperature to approximately 2 K, including setting up or operating suitable instrumentation, acquiring reliable measurements, troubleshooting and interpreting the results. Experience limited to post-processing data collected by others is not sufficient.

 

We expect a robust understanding of semiconductor transport and junction physics, including doping, carrier freeze-out, leakage, contact effects, admittance and interface/defect responses.

 

You should be able to distinguish genuine physical phenomena from contact, parasitic, instrumentation and other measurement artefacts through quantitative analysis of temperature-, bias- and frequency-dependent data.

 

You will also have substantial hands-on semiconductor materials characterisation experience, with practical competence in at least two complementary techniques among XTEM and HR-XRD, and the ability to interpret and correlate evidence from these methods.

 

Knowledge of AFM, SEM, FIB, SIMS, EDX, XRR, FTIR, or Hall effect measurements will be an advantage; expertise in every technique is not required.

 

Relevant Si/Ge/SiGe epitaxy, heterojunctions or cryogenic electronics experience would be particularly welcome.

 

You will be organised, collaborative, committed to safe and reproducible research, and able to communicate experimental methods, uncertainties and findings clearly.

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£35,302 per annum). Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£36,320 per annum).

About the Department

The Semiconductor Research Group investigates the epitaxial growth, characterisation, physics and applications of group-IV semiconductors, including Si, Ge and SiGe heterostructures. Its research combines advanced semiconductor materials synthesis with structural and electrical characterisation and international academic and industrial collaboration.

 

The Department of Physics is a vibrant research and teaching environment with over 200 academic, research, technical and professional services staff, more than 1000 undergraduate students and approximately 200 postgraduate researchers.

 

It is committed to equality of opportunity, mutual respect and inclusion, and holds an Athena SWAN Silver Award and an Institute of Physics Inclusion Award.

 

Further information about working in the Department and the benefits available can be found at: https://warwick.ac.uk/physics/staff/working/

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. 

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held in mid-January 2027.

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.

Job Title:  Research Associate in Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

As a Research Associate in the GATE (General Architecture for Text Engineering) team, you will conduct cutting-edge research in detecting and analysing online misinformation. Your work will advance explainable methods from machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to analyse false and misleading narratives spreading over time and online platforms, working in close collaboration with journalists and fact-checkers. You will also evaluate the accuracy of information provided by widely used chatbots (eg ChatGPT) and AI-generated search overviews. You will follow ethical and legal protocols, ensuring that the AI methods are reliable and robust to adversarial attacks.

Additionally, you will lead the write-up and publication of novel research in top-tier journals, present findings at leading international conferences, and collaborate with consortium partners to translate technical discoveries into actionable toolkits. Dedicated funding is provided for conference travel, journal publications, and high-impact stakeholder demonstrations.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

Apply natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyse online disinformation narratives in near-real-time social media streams.
Evaluate the accuracy of online chatbots and AI-generated search overviews.
Implement explainable, robust, and scalable narrative analysis tools capable of processing large-scale social media streams.
Set project milestones, test methodologies, maintain documentation, and ensure timely delivery of project deliverables.
Meet regularly with consortium partners, technical teams, and external stakeholders to align research with practical impact.
Publish novel techniques and findings in top-tier journals and present at relevant academic, industry, and policy conferences.
Collaborate effectively with researchers, PhD students, and technical staff across the department and partner organisations.
Deliver and undertake training in interdisciplinary research skills, including but not limited to NLP, machine learning, social media analysis, web service development and deployment, and computational social sciences.
Make ethical decisions in research activities – prioritising human rights, freedom of expression, and ethical AI principles – while embedding sustainability into daily work.
Carry out other duties commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

 

Person Specification

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and are respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply.

 Full time starting salary is normally in the range £36,636 to £46,049 with potential progression once in post to £48,822.

 Fixed Term contract up to November 2028 

 UK and International Travel may be required for this role. 

 Background 

 The Global Centre for Clean Energy and Equitable Transportation Solutions (CLEETS) is seeking a highly motivated researcher with a background in transport modelling and data analysis to join a successful and growing research team at the University of Birmingham. CLEETS is an international collaboration between leading universities in the UK and the USA, aimed at enabling a sustainable and equitable transition in energy and transport systems (see: https://www.cleets-global-center.org/). In the UK, the research is funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI). Within CLEETS, Dr Dilum Dissanayake leads the Travel Demand Management and Clean Energy and Connected Vehicle (CECV) Adoption task.

 Role Summary 

 Work within specified research grants and projects and contribute to writing bids. 

 Operate within area of specialism.

 Analyse and interpret research findings and results. 

 Contribute to generating funding. 

 Contribute to licensing or spin out deals with demonstrated commercial success (such as revenues, asset or company sales, IP generated) and/or public understanding of the discipline or similar.

 The successful candidate will join a multidisciplinary research team based at the University of Birmingham and will work closely with collaborators at Cardiff University and partner institutions in the USA. The primary aim of this role is to advance understanding of the societal impacts of transport decarbonisation strategies and energy system transitions in urban regions in both the United States (Great Lakes) and the United Kingdom (South Wales and the West Midlands). 
 The postholder will undertake travel demand analysis using attitudinal and stated preference data collected by the CLEETS team, with a focus on examining transport users’ awareness of environmental impacts and how this influences their adoption of sustainable travel choices. The role will also involve close engagement with a wide range of stakeholders to understand policy priorities at both regional and national levels.

 Candidates must provide a CV with publication list and a cover letter indicating their motivation for applying.
