Research Associate in Human-Robot Interaction

Job id: 161305. Salary: £45,031 - £48,607 per annum, including London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 21 October 2026. Closing date: 18 November 2026.

Business unit: Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sci. Department: Engineering.

Contact details: Dr Oya Celiktutan. oya.celiktutan@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Strand Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us

We are recruiting a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join CO-STAR (CO-designing Socially inTelligent Assistive Robots for Future Healthcare), a research programme bringing together King’s College London, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. CO-STAR aims to advance socially intelligent assistive robots for future healthcare, combining cutting-edge research in artificial intelligence and robotics with human-centred co-design and real-world clinical deployment. We are looking for a candidate who can join the project in January 2027 or soon thereafter.

The successful candidate will join the Department of Engineering at King’s College London and become a member of the Social AI & Robotics Lab (SAIR), led by Dr Oya Celiktutan. They will work closely with researchers, engineers, healthcare professionals, patients and other stakeholders at Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT), providing a unique opportunity to conduct cutting-edge robotics research in close partnership with a major NHS organisation.

SAIR conducts research in multimodal machine learning and human-centred embodied AI, with a particular focus on developing autonomous agents that can perceive, understand and interact effectively with humans. The lab’s research addresses challenges in multimodal perception, human behaviour understanding and forecasting, robot learning, navigation and manipulation, and socially aware human–robot interaction.

SAIR’s research has been supported by the Royal Academy of Engineering, EPSRC, the Royal Society, and EU Horizon programmes, as well as through industrial collaborations. The lab’s research has received several distinctions, including the Best Paper Award at IEEE RO-MAN 2022, the NVIDIA CCS Best Student Paper Award Runner-Up at IEEE FG 2021, and First Place and Honourable Mention Awards at the ICCV UDIVA Challenge 2021. 

About the role

Imagine a future where robots meaningfully assist people with limited mobility and support patients and clinicians across healthcare environments. Assistive robotics has the potential to transform independence, wellbeing, and the delivery of care. Advances in AI are rapidly expanding what robots can perceive, understand, and do, bringing this future closer than ever. Yet a critical gap remains between technical capability and real-world deployment: robots still struggle to understand human behaviour, adapt to complex social situations, and operate safely and appropriately alongside people. Using the hospital as a living lab to advance human–robot interaction and integration with clinical workflows, the CO-STAR project aims to bridge this gap.

CO-STAR will engineer the next generation of socially intelligent assistive robots that can interact naturally with people while meeting the demands of real-world healthcare environments. 

The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping and delivering the research programme, working across human–robot interaction, machine learning, socially intelligent AI, and healthcare robotics. They will contribute to the design, development, and evaluation of robotic and AI systems and work closely with the multidisciplinary CO-STAR team and Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust to translate research advances into real-world healthcare settings. Please refer to the Job Description for further details about the role and the required application documents.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

shape and conduct high-quality multidisciplinary research in collaboration with the CO-STAR project team;
develop novel research in human–robot interaction, machine learning, and socially intelligent robotics;
contribute to the design, development, implementation, and evaluation of robotic and AI systems within the scope of the project;
disseminate research findings through high-quality publications and presentations at leading international conferences and journals;
contribute to activities that maximise the academic, clinical, and societal impact of the research.

This is a full-time, fixed-term post for 21 months, with the potential for extension up to a total of 42 months, subject to funding arrangements. The desired start date is January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Application Documents

Please read and follow the application instructions carefully. Applications that do not comply with the requirements below, including the specified page limits, will not be considered. Please submit only the requested documents, as additional or unsolicited materials may also result in rejection.

1. Curriculum Vitae (maximum 2 pages): Provide an up-to-date academic CV detailing your qualifications, research experience, technical expertise, and relevant achievements. Include a complete list of publications at the end of your CV (excluded from the 2-page limit) and highlight up to three publications that best demonstrate your research contributions.

2. Supporting Statement (maximum 3 pages): In the context of the CO-STAR project, provide a structured statement demonstrating how you meet the essential and desirable criteria outlined in the Person Specification.

•       Address each criterion individually, using its corresponding title (e.g., Essential Criterion 1, Essential Criterion 2).

•       Essential Criteria: Address all six essential criteria individually, providing specific evidence and examples.

•       Desirable Criteria: Address all four desirable criteria individually, providing relevant evidence or explaining your motivation where applicable.

•       PhD Completion Status: If your PhD has not yet been awarded, clearly state your current stage of study, expected thesis submission date, anticipated viva date (if known), and expected date of completion.

Your responses should be concise, evidence-based, and relevant to the CO-STAR project. Avoid general statements without supporting examples.

3. Academic Referees: Provide the names and contact details of two academic referees, preferably including your current or most recent research supervisor. Please indicate whether they may be contacted informally before the interview.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates with the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

PhD awarded (or near completion*) in Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related discipline.
Strong research background in socially aware or human-centred AI, machine learning, robotics, and/or human–robot interaction.
Strong publication record in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and/or international conferences, such as ICRA, IROS, RA-L, CoRL, AAAI, NeurIPS, CVPR, HRI, or related venues, commensurate with career stage.
Excellent programming skills, particularly in Python, and hands-on experience with deep learning frameworks and models.
Practical experience with the Robot Operating System (ROS), physical robotic platforms, and/or robot simulation environments.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both academic and non-academic audiences.

Desirable criteria

Experience of collaborative research, particularly in multidisciplinary environments involving researchers, engineers, and other project stakeholders.
Experience with multimodal machine learning, foundation models, and/or neuro-symbolic AI approaches.
Experience conducting human–robot interaction studies or evaluating robotic systems with human participants.
Experience of, or strong motivation for, collaborating with healthcare professionals, patients, and other stakeholders in real-world clinical environments.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description 

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who are close to completing their PhD will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6. 

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university.

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

To find out how our managers will review your application, please take a look at our ‘How we Recruit’ pages.

 About the Role 

 The Semiconductor Research Group ( https://warwick.ac.uk/silicon ) in the Department of Physics at the University of Warwick is recruiting a Research Fellow with outstanding experimental skills in semiconductor materials science and cryogenic electrical characterisation. 

 The appointment supports a collaborative EPSRC–NSF project with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), USA: “Towards Ultralow-Noise SiGe Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors for Quantum Technology and Beyond: Epitaxial Engineering of Cryogenic Charge Transport.” 

 The research investigates how epitaxial layer design, alloy composition, strain, doping, interfaces and defects govern the electrical characteristics of SiGe heterojunctions and ultimately the cryogenic performance of SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs). 

 You will investigate Si/SiGe heterostructures grown using Warwick’s in-house reduced-pressure chemical vapour deposition (RP-CVD) facilities. 

 A defining element of the role is independently performing and interpreting current–voltage (I–V), capacitance–voltage (C–V) and conductance–voltage (G–V) measurements over temperatures from room temperature down to approximately 2 K. This includes assessment of bias-, frequency- and temperature-dependent effects, experimental artefacts, and the physical mechanisms responsible for non-ideal junction behaviour. 

 You will integrate these results with rigorous structural and materials characterisation, particularly cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (XTEM/TEM), high-resolution X-ray diffraction (HR-XRD), atomic force microscopy (AFM) and relevant complementary methods. 

 Your findings will inform the interpretation and optimisation of SiGe epitaxial heterostructures and provide the materials perspective for the international project team. 

 HBT device fabrication is undertaken by collaborators, not at Warwick. Where relevant, the role may include focused ion beam (FIB) specimen preparation and SEM/XTEM characterisation of collaborator-fabricated HBTs. 

 You will benefit from specialist semiconductor and low-temperature measurement facilities, scientific collaboration with Caltech and opportunities to publish and present internationally. 

 This is a laboratory-based experimental research position requiring full-time on-site working at the University of Warwick. The successful candidate will be expected to work in person within the Semiconductor Research Group's laboratories and research facilities. Due to the hands-on nature of the experimental activities, including specialist semiconductor materials characterisation and cryogenic electrical measurements, remote or hybrid working arrangements are not available for this position.

About the role

Advance Your Engineering Career Through Innovation and Impact

The Department of Mechanical Engineering is seeking to recruit a Postdoctoral Research Associate to investigate the fluid dynamics and heat transfer in rotating compressor cavities of gas turbines engines. The project is funded by the EPSRC in collaboration with the University of Surrey, Rolls-Royce and Siemens Energy. We are seeking a driven and capable individual to lead a high-impact project developing the next generation of hydrogen-compatible turbomachinery technology.

This position will offer you a way to apply your experience to a project that could shape the future of green energy technology and net-zero aerospace. As the Research Associate, you’ll lead a technically ambitious project with real-world application and long-term value. You’ll have the chance to:

Take ownership of a major research project to advance the understanding of fluid-dynamics and heat transfer through innovative experimental methods
Work at the intersection of academia and industry with support from both
Develop your skills in leadership, innovation, and strategic technical development
Gain access to training and a personal development allowance
Broaden your professional network through interaction with industrial partners

This role offers the autonomy of an academic position, with the added benefits of structured support and mentoring.

The goal is to investigate experimentally the buoyancy-induced rotating flow in a compressor cavity at low TRL. The research is underpinned by brand new instrumentation and to be conducted over a range of non-dimensional, engine-representative conditions. The study includes a fundamental exploration of boundary-layer transition from laminar to turbulent flow at high Grashof number. The experiments will be complemented by computational simulation at the University of Surrey, with the aim to scale data to higher TRL. The successful completion and implementation of this research will improve engine design methods at Rolls-Royce and Siemens for next-generation hydrogen-compatible engines.

About you

The ideal candidate will have:

A PhD in a relevant engineering field or experience in industrial R&D
Experience with experimentation and data analysis tools such as Matlab
Proficiency in CAD
Confidence working independently and engaging with multiple stakeholders

This role is offered on a full time (36.5 hours) fixed term basis with an expected duration of 36 months.

About Birmingham City University

At Birmingham City University, we are a diverse and inclusive learning community of over 31,400 students from more than 120 countries. We aim to become an exemplar anchor institution, creating and sharing knowledge for a better and more inclusive society. We are committed to providing a transformational educational experience, supporting world-class research, and fostering a collaborative and supportive working environment for our staff.

Recognised as one of the UK’s Top 250 employers (Financial Times & Statista), we pride ourselves on being a place where colleagues feel valued, supported, and able to grow their careers while contributing to the success of our students and communities.

Our student demographic reflects the rich cultural and ethnic diversity of Birmingham itself, with a significant proportion of students from minoritised ethnic backgrounds and the majority of our home students coming from the West Midlands. This diversity is a strength, and it calls for a workforce that is equipped to challenge deficit narratives and thinking — those assumptions that position students from underrepresented groups as lacking rather than recognising their assets, strengths and potential.

By embracing this perspective, we aim to create an environment where all students and colleagues can thrive, and where our work contributes positively to the social, cultural and economic life of Birmingham and beyond.

Role Summary

We are seeking a Post-Doctoral Researcher in Wind Assisted Ship Propulsion (UK National Clean Maritime Hub) to join our Department of Engineering, supporting the delivery of high-quality services across the University.

In this role, you will undertake leading research into the performance and application of wind-assisted ship propulsion technologies, contributing to the development of robust methods for assessing their potential to reduce ship energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. You will also contribute to BCU's commitments within the UK National Clean Maritime Research Hub, working with project partners to deliver high-quality research outputs, publications, technical guidance, and impact.

Key Responsibilities

Undertake research into wind-assisted ship propulsion and its contribution to maritime decarbonisation.
Develop and apply appropriate analytical, numerical, and/or performance-prediction methods.
Analyse ship and wind propulsion performance data and evaluate potential reductions in energy use and greenhouse gas emissions.
Contribute to the development and validation of methodologies for assessing wind-assisted propulsion technologies.
Work collaboratively with researchers across BCU, the UK National Clean Maritime Research Hub and relevant industry partners.
Prepare high-quality journal papers, conference papers, technical reports, and other research outputs.
Present research findings at project meetings, conferences, workshops, and stakeholder events.
Contribute to knowledge exchange and engagement with the maritime industry and other stakeholders.
Support the delivery of agreed project milestones and research outputs, with an opportunity to gain experience of supervising PhD and MRes students.
Contribute to the development of follow-on research proposals and opportunities arising from the project.

Essential Requirements

A PhD (or near completion), or equivalent research experience, in Naval Architecture, Marine Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Fluid Dynamics, or a closely related discipline.
Strong knowledge of engineering analysis, modelling, or performance prediction.
Experience of numerical modelling, computational methods, data analysis, or related engineering research methods.
Ability to undertake independent research and deliver high-quality research outputs.
Evidence of academic writing and the ability to communicate research findings clearly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary research team.
Good organisational skills and the ability to deliver work to agreed deadlines.

Desirable Requirements

Knowledge or experience of wind-assisted ship propulsion, ship performance, sailing aerodynamics, or marine renewable technologies.
Understanding of maritime decarbonisation and greenhouse gas reduction.
Experience of programming or engineering analysis software, for example Python, MATLAB, or equivalent.
Experience of publishing research in peer-reviewed journals.
Experience of working with industry or within collaborative research projects.
Awareness of international maritime environmental regulations and the evolving regulatory framework for shipping emissions.

Further Information

If you are excited by the opportunity to help shape the future of Clean Maritime and Wind Assisted Ship Propulsion, we would love to hear from you.

For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Prof JB Souppez at jb.souppez@bcu.ac.uk

Brunel University London was established in 1966 and is a leading multidisciplinary research-intensive technology university. For more information please visit: https://www.brunel.ac.uk/about/our-history/home 

The Department of Engineering delivers programmes in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electronic and Electrical Engineering, and Civil and Environmental Engineering. We are seeking to appoint a research assistant who will undertake research towards a PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering. The project objectives are to develop models for the design and analysis of turbo-compressors suitable for industrial high temperature heat pumps (IHTHPs). The focus will be on compressor system mechanical and electrical design considering sealing and cooling of components. The models will be validated using Finite Element and Thermal Analysis tools.

postings.listing_context: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Mathematical and Statistical Methods for Genome Privacy (Fixed Term) Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics £37,694-£46,049 Research 6 October 2026 31 October 2026 LE51229
postings.advert_text:
We invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Mathematical and Statistical Methods for Genome Privacy in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics at the University of Cambridge. The successful candidate will join the research group of Dr Gamze Gursoy and work on developing new mathematical and computational methods for privacy-preserving human pangenome references.

Human pangenome references provide increasingly rich representations of human genetic diversity, but their scale and structure also raise important questions about how information contributed by individuals can be protected. This project will develop new approaches at the intersection of graph algorithms, statistical methodology, optimization, privacy, and computational genomics, with the broader goal of enabling useful population-scale genomic references while limiting disclosure of sensitive information about the individuals represented within them.

Depending on the successful candidate's interests and background, research directions may include differentially private construction and analysis of pangenome graphs, privacy-aware graph algorithms and representations, statistical characterization of privacy-utility trade-offs, optimization of algorithms for large genomic graphs, and development and benchmarking of methods on human pangenome data. There will be considerable freedom for the successful candidate to help shape the scientific direction of the project.

We are particularly interested in candidates with a strong background in one or more of the following areas:
- statistics;
- graph theory or graph algorithms;
- mathematical or numerical optimization;
- differential privacy or related areas of data privacy;
- algorithms and theoretical computer science;
- computational genomics, bioinformatics, or pangenomics.

We do not expect candidates to be experts in all of these areas. Applicants with deep expertise in one area and a strong interest in learning and working across the others are strongly encouraged to apply. In particular, we welcome applications from statistics, mathematics, optimization, privacy, or algorithms who are excited about applying their methods to fundamental problems in human genomics, as well as researchers from computational genomics who are interested in developing expertise in privacy.

The project is highly interdisciplinary. The successful candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with Professor Po-Ling Loh in the Statistical Laboratory, Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics (DPMMS), particularly on statistical, optimization, and differential privacy aspects of the work. There will also be opportunities for interaction and collaboration with researchers in the broader Human Pangenome Project community.

The postholder will be expected to develop and manage their own research with guidance from the PI, contribute actively to the intellectual life of the research group, and communicate their work through publications, presentations, seminars, and conferences. They will join a collaborative group working broadly across computational genomics, statistical genetics, privacy-preserving computation, and trustworthy methods for genomic and biomedical data.

Applicants should have completed, or be close to completing, a PhD in statistics, mathematics, computer science, computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, or a related field. Evidence of strong quantitative, computational, or methodological research is more important than prior experience in any particular application area. Strong programming skills and an interest in interdisciplinary research are desirable.

The funding requires that candidates must not have been UK residents during the 24 months before the start date, nor be currently employed by a UK organisation or its overseas campuses.

The appointment is for two years in the first instance.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Please indicate the contact details (including their email addresses) of two academic referees on the online application form and upload a full curriculum vitae and a description of your recent research (not to exceed two pages). Please ensure that at least one of your referees is contactable at any time during the selection process and is made aware that they will be contacted by the Mathematics HR Office Administrator to request that they upload a reference for you to our Web Recruitment System; and please encourage them to do so promptly.

For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Gamze Gursoy at gg584@cam.ac.uk.

If you have any queries regarding the application process, please contact: LE51229@maths.cam.ac.uk.

Start date: As soon as possible, or by negotiation.

Interviews will be held soon after the closing date.

Please quote reference LE51229 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

This post is part of the EPSRC Programme Grant “Dialling Up Performance for On Demand Manufacturing”. This project aims to develop a TOOLKIT to enable the rapid formulation of 3D printable materials into products. This toolkit will be composed of an integrated suite of software and experimental tools and will be informed by the collection of data en route to the development of advanced 3D printed products. The focus of this specific role is the development of software tools that support the development of TOOLKIT: to develop and use optimisation techniques to determine new geometrical configurations suitable for a range of products. Initially this will be aimed at biocatalytic flow reactors, but it is anticipated that other applications may be considered. This is an interdisciplinary collaboration that will require working with researchers across engineering, catalysis, optimisation and computational modelling.

Your role will be to develop and advance the computational framework describing biocatalytic flow reactors to enable design optimisation to be performed, and new, more efficient designs to be proposed and manufactured. You will aid in writing publications, present research at national and international conferences and liaise with collaborators. You will be given support to develop and shape your future career, and hence this position may be particularly attractive to those looking to develop their research independence and leadership skills in a supportive and team-oriented environment.   

You must have (or about to complete) a PhD in engineering, physics or a related discipline. A demonstrable ability to use scientific languages and packages, such as Python or Matlab, is essential and a knowledge of 3D printing and related techniques is desirable. You will have good interpersonal skills and the ability of working in a team to tight deadlines. The CV and/or cover letter should clearly exemplify how you meet the criteria highlighted herein and in the Role Profile and describe your motivation for applying for this position.

The post is for a period of 18 months and is based in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Nottingham. The position is available from 1st November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.  We are seeking two full-time Postdoctoral Research Assistants in Machine Learning to join the Visual Geometry Group (VGG), in central Oxford. Each successful candidate will be assigned to one of these projects and will work under the supervision of Dr. João Henriques. Both posts are available for 12 months in the first instance.

The research will investigate how representations of 3D geometry and motion can help robots manipulate a wide range of objects, including deformable objects, and generalise to new settings. The methods will be evaluated on robotic manipulation tasks, including experiments on real robots.

Job Title:  Research Associate in Speech and Acoustic Sensing for Respiratory Health
Posting Start Date:  24/09/2026
Job Id:  3040

Work Arrangement:  Full Time (Hybrid)
Contract Type:  Fixed-term

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

We are seeking a postdoctoral research associate to join LungSight, a multidisciplinary project developing low-cost, non-invasive audio-visual AI for earlier identification of chronic lung disease. The project aims to support a shift from reactive, clinic-based diagnosis towards proactive home screening using everyday devices such as smartphones, tablets and home computers.

Based in the School of Computer Science at the University of Sheffield, you will lead the machine learning research on acoustic foundation models for respiratory health. You will work with large-scale real-world recordings of speech, breathing and cough, developing self-supervised learning and foundation-model approaches that are robust to noise, demographic variation and different recording environments. You will also contribute to clinically informed acoustic biomarkers and to the integration of audio with visual and clinical information.

LungSight is a multi-university collaboration involving collaborators from the Manchester Metropolitan University, the University of Southampton, the University of Cambridge, the University of Leicester and the University of Leeds, alongside NHS and third-sector partners. This post will work particularly closely with a complementary PDRA at Southampton, whose research will focus more strongly on clinically informed acoustic feature engineering, while the Sheffield post has a stronger machine learning and representation learning focus. The role offers opportunities for high-quality publications, open research outputs, clinical and stakeholder engagement, and career development at the interface of AI and healthcare.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

Develop and evaluate domain-adapted acoustic foundation models for respiratory health using speech, breathing and cough recordings.
Curate, pre-process and analyse large-scale real-world audio datasets, including sensitive healthcare and helpline recordings processed within appropriate secure data environments.
Investigate state-of-the-art self-supervised learning approaches, including Transformer-based architectures, masked prediction and contrastive learning, for robust respiratory acoustic representation learning.
Fine-tune and validate models on labelled respiratory datasets and clinically relevant downstream tasks, assessing accuracy, generalisability and clinical utility.
Investigate potential confounding factors, demographic bias, background-noise effects and domain shift, and develop methods that improve trustworthy and equitable model performance.
Contribute to clinically informed acoustic modelling, working closely with the Southampton PDRA, who will lead complementary feature-engineering research; investigate how engineered physiological features can be combined with learned representations from the Sheffield machine-learning work.
Collaborate with project researchers to develop multimodal approaches combining acoustic, visual and clinical information for respiratory disease screening.
Work closely with researchers across the LungSight consortium, including Manchester Metropolitan University, Southampton, Cambridge, Leicester and Leeds, as well as clinical, NHS, patient/public and third-sector partners; participate in project meetings, joint research activities and dissemination.

 We are inviting applications for a Research Associate to support the University of Sheffield’s contribution to the SMART (Secure Motor AI-Responsive Technology) project funded by Innovate UK. The post will contribute to the development and validation of computationally efficient motor-twin models for permanent magnet synchronous machines. The work will focus on machine modelling, parameter and state estimation, plus preparing modelling outputs that can be shared with project’s partners.

 The successful candidate will work with academic and industrial project partners to generate simulation and experimental validation evidence, using available machine data, dynamometer testing, and HIL methods. The role will also involve documenting methods and results for project deliverables, reports and publications.

 The post is suited to candidates with a PhD awarded, in electrical machines, drives, control, real-time simulation, or a closely related engineering discipline, who is motivated to develop deployable motor-twin methods for intelligent motor drives.
 The contract end date of this post is 31st January 2028.

 The School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) belongs to the prestigious Faculty of Engineering. We are one of the largest academic communities of engineers in the UK, ranked joint 1st for Research Environment in the last Research Excellence Framework (REF 2021)! Our specific field (EEE) is also ranked very highly, which is a marker of our excellence and ambition (QS 2024: 11th in UK, The Guardian 2024: 3rd, The Times Higher 2024: 7th in the UK).

 We are home to several national institutes and centres, for example:

 The National 6G Radio Systems Facility,

 We strive to conduct fundamental research and innovation to address global challenges, as well as support the education of the next generation of engineers.

 The University of Sheffield is a remarkable and inclusive place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

 We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a generous annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pension scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more.

 Find out more at sheffield.ac.uk/jobs/benefits and join us to become part of something special.

 We build teams of people from different heritages and lifestyles from across the world, whose talent and contributions complement each other to greatest effect. We believe diversity in all its forms delivers greater impact through research, teaching and student experience.

 About us 

 UCL Department of Chemical Engineering is one of the top research and teaching departments in the UK and has world-class standing. The department offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, and has an extensive research portfolio across a wealth of areas, from molecular scale to complex systems.

 About the role 

 The successful candidate will develop and operate high-throughput computational screening workflows for MOFs, integrating molecular simulation, automated structure generation and large-scale materials databases. The post holder will lead computational research on the design, screening and optimisation of MOFs for target adsorption applications. In addition, the successful candidate will perform advanced molecular simulations of adsorption, including quantum calculations, grand-canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) and molecular dynamics (MD), to characterise and predict the performance of candidate materials.

 Salary is £47,186-£ 50,942 per annum inclusive of London allowance.

 This is a fixed-term role until 31st of December 2029 in the first instance.

 About you 

 The successful candidate will hold (or shortly expect to obtain) a Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Physics, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science or a related quantitative discipline (or equivalent industry experience), together with an undergraduate degree (2(i) minimum) or M.Sc. in a relevant field. The post holder will have demonstrable experience with atomistic/molecular simulation methods, alongside knowledge of nanoporous materials (e.g. MOFs, zeolites or porous polymers) and adsorption processes for gas capture, with experience or knowledge of material informatics and the analysis of large materials datasets. Demonstrable experience or knowledge of computational modelling and data-driven approaches, including machine learning methods, optimisation techniques, and relevant programming skills is essential.

 What we offer 

 As well as exciting opportunities, UCL offers a range of great benefits. Find out more: UCL Rewards and Benefits .

 About us 

 The “ Next-Gen Biopharma Manufacturing 5.0 ” Prosperity Partnership is a 5-year collaborative programme between UCL Biochemical Engineering and AstraZeneca, jointly funded by EPSRC and AstraZeneca. It aims to transform antibody manufacturing using AI, automation, digital twins and advanced analytics to improve production of therapies for cancer, obesity and autoimmune conditions. Delivered through the UCL–AstraZeneca Centre of Excellence, the programme will appoint six postdoctoral researchers to work across UCL and AstraZeneca sites, combining computational and experimental approaches.

 UCL Biochemical Engineering is a global leader in bioprocess engineering research and education, with a mission to develop innovative biomanufacturing solutions for health and a sustainable bioeconomy. The department combines world-class facilities, strong industrial links, and an interdisciplinary research culture. AstraZeneca is a global, science-led biopharmaceutical company with a focus on the discovery, development, and commercialisation of medicines in Oncology, Rare Diseases, and BioPharmaceuticals.

 About the role 

 We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join this ambitious Prosperity Partnership between UCL and AstraZeneca and work in a cross-disciplinary team across both UCL (London) and AstraZeneca (Cambridge) sites. This role will evaluate the economic and environmental impact of next-generation biomanufacturing technologies, supporting more sustainable and cost-effective development pathways for advanced biologics through data-driven decision-making.

 You will lead the development of integrated techno-economic and life cycle assessment models, incorporating uncertainty analysis and multi-objective optimisation to evaluate and optimise the cost, carbon footprint and resource impacts of emerging bioprocess strategies. These decision-support tools will be applied to real-world case studies in collaboration with AstraZeneca, generating insights that inform strategic choices and guide industrial implementation.

 This role is funded for 2 years in the first instance, with potential for extension.

 About you 

 You will hold (or be near completion of) a PhD in a relevant discipline such as biochemical engineering, chemical engineering, industrial engineering, environmental sustainability, or a related field. Essential to this role is demonstrated expertise in both techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment, supported by strong quantitative modelling and analytical skills.

 While prior experience in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical sector would be beneficial, it is not essential.You will have experience working on interdisciplinary research projects and be motivated to deliver practical, real-world impact. Excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach are essential, as is the ability to work independently and take ownership of your research. Experience developing decision-support tools, familiarity with LCA software, and skills in optimisation and uncertainty analysis would be advantageous. Commitment to UCL's values and to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion is essential.

 What we offer

Role Description

The Centre for Reviews and Dissemination (CRD) at the University of York is recruiting a Grade 6 or Grade 7 Research Fellow in Health Economics.

CRD is a world-leading academic research department specialising in evidence synthesis and health technology assessment (HTA). Our work spans a broad range of health and public health areas, providing high-quality evidence to inform national policy and practice decisions.

The successful candidate will work primarily within our Technology Assessment Review (TAR) programme, undertaking research to support National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) decision-making as part of the York External Assessment Group (EAG). You will also contribute to our NIHR Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG) programme and broader health economic modelling projects across CRD, with scope to develop your own research interests.

We welcome applications from candidates with a relevant Master’s degree and/or PhD (or equivalent experience) in health economics or another quantitative discipline, such as applied statistics or mathematics. Candidates must possess strong quantitative skills, a comprehensive knowledge of health economics and cost-effectiveness analysis, and a good understanding of HTA, systematic reviews, and meta-analysis.

Candidates applying for Grade 7 must additionally have experience of critiquing, conceptualising, and constructing health economic decision models in an HTA context, as well as proven ability to lead research elements and supervise early-career researchers. Familiarity with UK health systems and research funding is desirable. Further training and career development will be supported.

CRD offers a friendly, supportive environment and holds a Silver Athena SWAN award. We embrace hybrid and flexible working (minimum 0.8 FTE / 4 days per week). This is an open-ended full-time position. We actively encourage applications from underrepresented groups, particularly Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic candidates.

Please state on your application whether you are applying for Grade 6 or Grade 7.

Interview date: To be confirmed

Informal enquiries: Contact Matthew Walton (matthew.walton@york.ac.uk), Ash Bullement (ash.bullement@york.ac.uk), or Professor Sofia Dias (sofia.dias@york.ac.uk).

The University strives to be diverse and inclusive  – a place where we can ALL be ourselves.

About the role

Join our thriving Centre of Excellence in Water-Based Systems for Health Protection and Department of Chemistry as a Prize Fellow in Biological Chemistry.

The Centre of Excellence in Water-Based Early-Warning Systems for Health Protection (CWBE) is a £13m interdisciplinary research centre, established in 2024 with funding from Research England’s Expanding Excellence in England (E3) scheme, together with contributions from the University of Bath and partners. 

We are working to transform public and environmental health management, establishing the first Urban Living Lab facility; a state-of-the-art digital water sensing platform, training base and ideas hub. Our ambition is to provide a practical roadmap for a UK early-warning system, co-produced with regional and national stakeholders to serve as a sentinel and multigenerational testing site for research and innovation. This platform will enable testing of public health and environmental interventions focused on increasing community resilience to disease, pollution and climate change impacts. 

We are looking to recruit a Prize Fellow:
To develop an internationally leading independent research programme in the broad areas of Biological chemistry; Chemical toxicology; Cheminformatics/data science. 
To teach aspects of analytical chemistry in both lectures and laboratory classes, maintaining the University’s high standards in teaching and learning, and its inclusive and supportive learning environment. 
To contribute, with support, at an appropriate level to the administration, leadership, and management of the Department’s and Centre’s activities. 
About you

At Bath we offer an exceptional environment for research teaching and learning and we wish to support you in reaching your potential for internationally leading research, in the broad field of water-based epidemiology. Applications are invited for a Prize Fellow position in the Department of Chemistry to join the multidisciplinary CWBE team, working on wastewater-based early warning systems for public health protection.

The successful candidate will develop an independent research programme aligned with the CWBE mission while expanding the Centre's existing capabilities in one or more of the following areas: Biological chemistry, Chemical Toxicology, Cheminformatics and Data Science. We are particularly interested in strengthening our expertise in proteomics, as well as in cheminformatics, artificial intelligence, and data science. Applicants should have expertise in at least one or two of these areas demonstrate the ability to work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary environment. The role will involve close interaction with engineers, chemists, biologists, and social scientists, making strong teamwork and communication skills essential.

You should hold a PhD and be able to demonstrate the potential to develop an internationally leading research programme, to acquire significant funding from UK and international sources, and to produce high-quality publications.

Application Requirements & Selection Process:

Please provide both research and teaching statements of up to two pages for each in addition to a full CV. 

Your research statement needs to outline your plans and intentions for research activity that expands and complements existing capabilities in the centre, grant capture over the coming five years and your planned contributions to further development of the centre. This document will be treated in the strictest confidence and with full respect for ownership. The teaching vision should outline your areas of teaching expertise and a range of potential teaching subjects as well as course development interests. These are mandatory components of the selection process, without which we will be unable to progress your application.

For informal discussion about the role, please contact Professor Matthew Jones, Head of Department (mj205@bath.ac.uk), Prof Barbara Kasprzyk-Hordern, Director of CWBE (bkh20@bath.ac.uk). However, please submit your application via the University website. This role is a full-time fixed term position (36.5 hours per week for 24 months). Subject to satisfactory progress at the end of the fixed term, the position will transfer to a Lectureship in the Department of Chemistry and CWBE. 

We consider ourselves to be a university where difference is celebrated, respected and encouraged. We have an excellent international reputation with staff from over 60 different nations and have made a positive commitment towards gender equity and intersectionality receiving a Silver Athena SWAN award. We truly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds will lead to a better environment for our employees and students and encourage applications from all genders, backgrounds, and communities, particularly from under-represented groups, and value the positive impact that will have on the university. We are committed to maintaining a safe and secure environment for our students, staff, and community by reinforcing our Safer Recruitment commitment.

We're very proud to be a signatory of the Armed Forces Covenant. an accredited Disability Confident Leader; autism friendly university, committed to building disability confidence and supporting disabled staff.

Heilbronn Research Fellowships in Pure Mathematics, Data Science, and Quantum Computing
The role

The Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research invites applications for Heilbronn Research Fellowships. Fellows divide their time equally between their own research and the classified research programme of the Heilbronn Institute. Research areas of interest include, but are not restricted to, Algebra, Algebraic Geometry, Combinatorics, Data Science, Number Theory, Probability, and Quantum Computing. Fellows have previously been appointed with backgrounds in most areas of Pure Mathematics and Statistics, and Mathematical/Theoretical Physics.

We expect to make up to 10 appointments at the University of Bristol, Imperial College London, King’s College London, UCL, and the University of Manchester. These appointments will mainly be in Pure Mathematics with up to two of the appointments at the University of Bristol in Data Science or Quantum Computing.

The salary range is £46,874 - £52,517 (or local equivalent) depending on previous experience, plus the London weighting where appropriate. There is a salary supplement of £3.5K pa, in recognition of the distinctive nature of these Fellowships. Payment of this supplement is conditional on a PhD thesis having been accepted in final form.

The positions are 3 years with fixed-term funding until 2030 with a preferred start date of 1 October 2027. Extensions of up to three years may be available, which can be held at a wider range of universities in the UK.

What will you be doing?

Fellows divide their time equally between their own research and the classified research programme of the Heilbronn Institute, thus enjoying opportunities to engage in collaborative work as well as individual projects.

Fellows join a cohort of around 50 Heilbronn Research Fellows that includes some of the leading early-career mathematicians in the UK. Expert mentoring will be provided by the host department, with a national programme of career development events overseen by our Associate Chairs, who are based in the School of Mathematics at the University of Bristol, Imperial College, and the University of Manchester.

The internal research programme is determined by the Head of HIMR in conjunction with GCHQ. Fellows are presented with a range of challenging mathematical problems and are given the facilities and support to contribute to one or more of them, frequently as part of a collaborative team.

You should apply if

Due to the nature of the Institute's work, Fellows must apply for a national security clearance at an appropriate level before appointment. Applications are open only to UK residents who are UK, or dual UK nationals: applicants are welcome to contact the Heilbronn Manager at himr-recruitment@bristol.ac.uk to discuss eligibility before applying.

The Heilbronn Institute is a supporter of the LMS Good Practice Scheme aimed at advancing women’s careers in mathematics and we particularly welcome applications from women.

Additional information

Applications will be made through mathjobs.org

Applicants will need to submit a cover letter, indicating the institutions where they prefer to hold their Fellowship from the above list of partner universities. In addition, we require a CV and a one-page statement of external research objectives over the 3 year Fellowship term. Applicants must arrange for three letters of reference to be uploaded to the mathjobs.org website, prior to the closing date.

The application deadline is 11.59pm GMT, Sunday 8th November 2026.

We anticipate holding interviews over the 11th - 14th of January 2027. 

For informal queries please contact: himr-recruitment@bristol.ac.uk 

Our strategy and mission

 

We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values.

BNU is a Disability Confident employer and as such you will be given the opportunity to declare a disability as part of the application process.

 

JOB DESCRIPTION

 

Job Title:  Research Assistant (Cloud-Based AI)

College/Professional Service:  College of Creative Arts, Technology and Engineering

	

Grade:  E

Location:  High Wycombe Campus / Hybrid

	

Hours:  84 hrs in total from Nov 26 to Jul 27

Responsible to:  Project Lead

Responsible for:  No line management needed

Job Purpose:

To support delivery of the funded research project ‘Cloud-Based Smart Digital Twin for Predictive Calibration Management of Weighing Instruments’, by designing, developing and implementing a cloud-based digital twin system that combines mechanical engineering knowledge, AWS cloud architecture and AI/ML techniques to predict and manage the calibration of weighing and measurement instruments.

 

 

Main Duties & Responsibilities of the role:

Design and implement a complete cloud-based system on Amazon Web Services (AWS) to support the digital twin project, covering architecture, development, deployment and maintenance.
Apply mechanical engineering principles, including sensor behaviour, material degradation and calibration processes, to inform the design of the digital twin model for weighing and measurement instruments.
Develop and apply Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to build predictive capabilities, such as fault prediction, condition-based maintenance and optimisation.
Write and maintain robust, well-documented code, primarily in Python, to support system development and data analysis.
Collect and record the data required from weighing scales (e.g. sensor readings, load and calibration data) to support model development, testing and validation of the digital twin.
Investigate and, where appropriate, implement AWS IoT TwinMaker or similar digital twin platforms to realise the smart digital twin functionality.
Use MATLAB or similar simulation and modelling tools to validate system performance and calibration predictions, where required.
Contribute to the testing, validation and continuous improvement of the predictive calibration management system.
Prepare technical documentation, reports and presentations summarising project progress, methodology and results for the research team and funders.
Collaborate effectively with academic supervisors, project partners and other researchers to ensure timely delivery of project milestones.
Comply with relevant legislative and other requirements (e.g., the Data Protection Act 2018 and GDPR; Health and Safety; UKVI; and Equality and Diversity) in all working practices.

Applications are invited for an experimental postdoctoral researcher to create architected materials using protein guided assembly in micro-emulsion templates. The researcher will be part of the NanoManufacturing group in the Department of Engineering at the University of Cambridge (http://www.nanomanufacturing.eng.cam.ac.uk/), which looks at various aspects of nanotechnology and manufacturing processes as well as energy storage systems. This work will be carried out in close collaboration with other leading research teams in Cambridge as well as Liverpool and the Netherlands. Collaborating with these groups will create a stimulating work environment with exciting opportunities for personal development and learning about different fields of research. This is a diverse team that values collaboration, scientific excellence and research integrity and the project's goal is to reduce our reliance on rare earths and critical minerals in Li-Ion battery cathodes and magnets.

The selected candidate will play a key role in the development of scalable droplet generation tools such as membrane emulsification and ink-jet printing as templates for protein guided assembly and bio-mineralisation. These structured materials will then be evaluated in Li-ion batteries, which is a research area in which the host group specialises. We will consider candidates with various research backgrounds including physical chemistry, engineering and material science. We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in emulsion-templating, colloidal self-assembly, and/or Li-ion batteries. Applicants are required to have a PhD or being close to obtaining a PhD.

Appointment at Research Associate level is dependent on having a PhD.

Those who have submitted but not yet received their PhD will be appointed at Research Assistant level, which will be amended to Research Associate once the PhD has been awarded.

Salary Ranges: Research Assistant: £33,002 - £35,608 Research Associate: £37,694 - £46,049

Fixed-term: The funding is for 18 months or through until 01/03/2028, whichever of these comes soonest.

 Department 

 The School of Computer Science and Electronic Engineering has a strong, internationally recognised research profile spanning artificial intelligence, machine learning and biomedical signal processing. The School hosts active research in neurotechnology and brain-computer interfacing, and provides access to substantial computing resources, including a GPU-enabled high-performance computing cluster. This post sits within PaiNeuro, an interdisciplinary project working towards objective pain measurement using neurophysiological signals, in collaboration with Vestre Viken Hospital Trust in Norway.   

 Duties of the Role 

 Working under the direction of the Principal Investigator, Dr Sebastian Halder, the post holder will carry out the advanced computational analysis for the project, developing and evaluating machine-learning methods that distinguish pain-related from pain-free states in clinical EEG, with particular emphasis on models that generalise to previously unseen participants. Specifically, the post holder will:

 Develop and maintain reproducible EEG preprocessing, artefact-handling and feature-extraction workflows.

 Implement and compare deep-learning approaches for EEG-based pain prediction, including architectures that capture spatial and temporal structure in the data.

 Develop Riemannian geometry-based methods using EEG covariance representations.

 Investigate cross-participant generalisation, including transfer learning, domain alignment and one-class classification approaches based on pain-free EEG.

 Validate models rigorously using held-out participant data and report performance using appropriate classification metrics.

 Contribute to scientific publications, open-source software, data documentation and the public release of code and curated data.

 Work closely with the Principal Investigator and the clinical collaborators in Norway, contributing to regular interdisciplinary project meetings.

 Skills and qualifications required 

 Applicants will have, or be close to completing, a PhD in computer science, electronic engineering, biomedical engineering, neuroscience, machine learning or a closely related discipline. The following are essential:

 Strong Python programming skills and experience with scientific-computing and machine-learning libraries.

 Experience applying machine learning, including deep learning, to EEG or other high-dimensional biosignals.

 A sound understanding of robust model evaluation, including participant-level cross-validation and testing on independent data.

 The ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary research team.

 Strong academic writing and spoken communication skills.

 The following are desirable:

 Experience with deep-learning architectures for time series or neural signals, such as convolutional or recurrent networks.

 Experience with Riemannian geometry methods for covariance-based signal classification.

 Knowledge of transfer learning, domain adaptation or one-class classification and anomaly detection.

 Familiarity with tools such as MNE-Python, PyTorch, Braindecode or pyRiemann.

 Experience working with clinical data, research governance and open, reproducible research practices.

Research Associate in Neurotechnology and Bioelectronic Devices
Apply now

ENG04038

About the role

Funded by the UK Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA) through its Massively Scalable Neurotechnology Programme, this Research Associate position will contribute to an ambitious interdisciplinary project developing novel bioelectronic technologies for minimally invasive neural monitoring. The successful candidate will play a leading role in the design, fabrication, integration and characterisation of advanced bioelectronic devices and experimental platforms. The role will involve device development, system integration, electrophysiological and acoustic testing, signal acquisition and analysis, and close collaboration with researchers in bioengineering, ultrasonics, neuroscience, robotics and computational modelling. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the interface of bioelectronics, neuroscience and advanced sensing technologies, contributing to the development of next-generation neurotechnology platforms. 

What you would be doing

You will contribute to the development, fabrication and evaluation of novel bioelectronic devices and experimental platforms for physiological signal sensing and analysis. Working within a highly interdisciplinary team spanning bioengineering, ultrasonics, neuroscience and advanced manufacturing, your responsibilities will include: 

Designing, fabricating and characterising novel bioelectronic devices and prototypes.
Developing device fabrication, assembly and integration workflows.
Establishing electrical, electrochemical and acoustic testing methodologies. 
Building and maintaining experimental platforms for device evaluation and validation.
Acquiring, processing and analysing physiological, electrical and acoustic signals. 
Evaluating device performance, sensitivity, stability and reliability.
Contributing to system integration and prototype optimisation.
Working closely with collaborators across multiple work packages to deliver bespoke devices and testing solutions.
Supporting laboratory-based validation studies where appropriate.
Maintaining accurate and complete experimental records.
Contributing to project milestones, technical reports and research deliverables.
Presenting research findings at project meetings and scientific conferences.
Publishing research in high-quality peer-reviewed journals.
Supporting student supervision and the preparation of research funding applications.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a motivated and collaborative researcher with experience in bioelectronics, biomedical devices, advanced sensing technologies, or a closely related area. You should have: 

A PhD, or equivalent research experience, in bioengineering, biomedical engineering, electronic engineering, materials science, physics, neuroscience, or a related discipline.
Experience in the fabrication, integration or characterisation of bioelectronic devices, sensors, or related technologies.
Experience in electrical, electrochemical, acoustic, or other experimental device characterisation techniques.
Experience in experimental data acquisition and quantitative data analysis.
Experience with signal processing and data interpretation.
The ability to troubleshoot complex experimental systems.
The ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Strong organisational, communication and scientific writing skills.
A publication record appropriate to career stage.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be advantageous: 

Bioelectronic devices, implantable technologies, or advanced sensing systems.
Device fabrication, advanced manufacturing, microfabrication, additive manufacturing, 3D printing, or related technologies.
Electrophysiological, electrochemical, acoustic or ultrasonic measurement techniques.
Signal processing, computational analysis or quantitative modelling of experimental data.
In vitro or animal research experience and associated experimental procedures.

Experience working in interdisciplinary teams spanning engineering, physical sciences, life sciences or clinical research.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to contribute to an ambitious ARIA-funded neurotechnology project at a world-leading institution and support Imperial’s mission to use science for humanity. 
A collaborative, multidisciplinary working environment spanning design engineering, bioengineering, mechanical engineering, and brain sciences.   
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. 
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. 
As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects 
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). 
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. 

Further information

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week) on a fixed-term contract for 24 months. An extension to 30 months is anticipated, subject to satisfactory progress and the availability of funding.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr Yunlong Zhao- yunlong.zhao@imperial.ac.uk.

About the role

Biochemical/biophysical research in a field-leading team on one of the hottest areas of photosynthesis research: the recently discovered, low-energy chlorophyll-f variants of the photosystems. Structure/function studies on this system have provided surprises and a new angle from which to view and understand oxygenic photosynthesis: the process that puts the energy into the biosphere.

What you would be doing

You will use a combination of interdisciplinary methods to solve the current burning questions in the field. These methods include biochemistry, biophysics, spectroscopy, molecular bioenergetics, redox methods, structural biology (e.g., cryo-EM), molecular biology, molecular enzymology, evolutionary considerations, and comparative work with other photosystems and other reaction centres.

You will have the opportunity not only to assimilate in-house expertise but also to gain further experience through collaborative work (on theory, computational chemistry, other spectroscopies, etc) elsewhere in Imperial, the UK, and abroad. The team’s energy accounting expertise has also allowed insights useful for energy policy; you are welcome to contribute to these activities.

What we are looking for

Ideally, you would have specific experience of the subject, as described below and in the job description as being “desirable”.

Practical experience of biophysical methods on the photosystems and or bioenergetic complexes (spectroscopy, electrochemical approaches, structural approaches, etc).
Practical experience in isolation and characterisation of the membrane protein complexes of bioenergetics.
Practical experience in microbiology and molecular biology of cyanobacteria.

However, excellent candidates with less direct experience of the specific field or with other relevant expertise will be considered (see job description).

What we can offer you

The opportunity to work in a world leading group on what is arguably the hottest subject in the field: long wavelength oxygenic photosynthesis.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant. 

The candidate is expected to start preferably before February 2027.

The team is currently 3 grad students, 2 post docs, 2 staff, 1 technician/lab manager, usually a few masters and UG students. We share lab facilities and office space with 3 other groups with related interests and other expertise. We work closely with a group in physics on theory and experiments and have several established collaborations with other spectroscopy and theory groups in the UK and abroad.

(Some relevant publications from the team DOI: 10.1126/science.aar8313, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.79890, https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-025-08326-y, DOI: 10.1126/science.ado6830, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73964-7).   

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: A.W. Rutherford and Andrea Fantuzzi – a.rutherford@imperial.ac.uk and a.fantuzzi@imperial.ac.uk. Be sure to put “Far-red PS Post Doc position” as the subject please.

About the role

You will play a key role in a multidisciplinary programme on computational proteomics in a new physical dimension, supported by UKRI and the NSF, involving Imperial College London (Physics), the University of California San Diego (Computing), as well as industrial and academic partners in Europe and the US. The programme aims to develop conceptually new de novo sequencing tools based on two-dimensional partial covariance mass spectrometry, invented and developed in the Department of Physics at Imperial College London. This role offers a unique opportunity for a physicist interested in developing transformative analytical technologies.

What you would be doing

This role combines computational and experimental aspects. You will design and implement advanced computational algorithms for reconstructing peptide sequences directly from experimental mass spectral data, without recourse to protein sequence databases. You will also be engaged in mass spectral data acquisition in an analytical mass spectrometry laboratory.

You will work collaboratively with the Imperial College team and US project partners on the development and optimisation of de novo sequencing algorithms. You will liaise with project partners and participate in data acquisition campaigns in partner laboratories.

What we are looking for

You will hold a PhD in Physics (or a closely related quantitative discipline) and have an outstanding record of research achievement. We are particularly interested in candidates with exceptional computational and analytical skills, demonstrated through the development of novel algorithms, advanced data-analysis methodologies, scientific software, machine learning approaches or other computational research tools.

The ideal candidate will be intellectually ambitious, highly self-motivated and excited by the prospect of working at the boundary between physics, computation and biomolecular science. Experience in proteomics or mass spectrometry is not required; candidates with strong backgrounds in computational physics, statistical physics, machine learning, signal processing, inverse problems, optimisation, applied mathematics or related fields are particularly encouraged to apply.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to contribute to a pioneering international research programme aimed at establishing an entirely new physical paradigm for biomolecular sequencing. You will help develop both the underlying physical methodology and the computational frameworks required to unlock information inaccessible to conventional analytical approaches, creating new capabilities with broad scientific and technological impact.
Collaboration within a multidisciplinary team involving physicists, computer scientists and analytical mass spectrometrists.
Involvement in publications, conference presentations and future grant applications.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and contribute to our mission of “Science for Humanity”.
Access to Imperial’s sector-leading career support for researchers, as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
A sector-leading salary and remuneration package, including 41 days’ leave per year and generous pension schemes.
A diverse, inclusive and collaborative working culture, with staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

The position is available immediately. We would ideally like the successful candidate to start as soon as possible, but the start date is flexible and can be agreed to accommodate notice periods and other commitments.

This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term role based at our South Kensington Campus.

If you require further details about the role, please contact:
Professor Vitali Averbukh – v.averbukh@imperial.ac.uk

About the role
We are looking for a Stakeholder Engagement Specialist to support engagement and knowledge exchange activities within the CIRCARB programme in the University of Leicester’s School of Engineering. Working closely with the Principal Investigator, Project Manager and wider project team, you will engage organisations across industry, academia, policy and related sectors, helping to communicate the programme’s activities, findings and opportunities.

You will help develop and maintain external relationships, coordinate stakeholder meetings, workshops, consultations and dissemination events, and gather feedback to inform the project team. You will also maintain records of engagement and follow-up actions, contribute to knowledge exchange and impact activity, and undertake relevant professional development. You will join an internationally recognised engineering environment with expertise spanning areas including green energy, transport and digital manufacturing, and with established links to major engineering companies.
About you
You will have a bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant professional experience, together with experience in stakeholder engagement, knowledge exchange, communications, business engagement or a related field. You will also have worked successfully with external organisations or stakeholders. Experience gained within research, innovation, sustainability, energy, manufacturing or industrial decarbonisation projects would be advantageous, as would experience of university-industry collaboration.

An excellent written and verbal communicator, you will be able to build effective professional relationships and engage confidently with people from different backgrounds. You will organise and prioritise activities within agreed timescales, work independently and make a positive contribution to a wider project team. A proactive, collaborative and professional approach will be essential to supporting the successful delivery and wider impact of CIRCARB.
Additional information
Informal enquiries are welcome and can be made to Muhammad Imran, Professor of Sustainable Energy Systems, mi263@leicester.ac.uk
 
As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role will also be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Please ensure this is discussed with your line manager prior to applying. More information regarding secondments can be found here.
 
The University of Leicester has been changing the world, and changing people’s lives, for 100 years. When you join us, you’ll become part of a community of Citizens of Change, which includes not only our staff and our current students but also thousands of Leicester graduates around the world.
 
As a diverse and forward-thinking employer, we embed the principles of equity, diversity and inclusion into everything we do. That includes not just our core missions of teaching and research, but also our support for staff, students and our local community through our values of Inspiring, Impactful and Inclusive.
 
We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond. We offer a competitive salary package, excellent pension scheme and a generous annual leave allowance, along with opportunities to develop your career in a supportive and collaborative environment.

Research Coordinator in Accelerator Science

 University of Liverpool 

 - Faculty of Science and Engineering - School of Physical Sciences - Department of Physics

 Liverpool

 Full Time

 Permanent
