 19th October 2026 

 Closes: 
 9th November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 117833 

 A permanent position as Research Coordinator in the Accelerator Science cluster at Liverpool University is available. The role will be based at the Cockcroft Institute on Daresbury Science and Innovation Campus and make substantial contributions to the research portfolio of the pan-European QUASAR Group. It will focus on the development and experimental exploitation of particle accelerators and light sources, and we are looking for an outstanding accelerator expert to strengthen our team and complement our existing expertise. Applicants are expected to have an internationally recognized researcher profile and make major contributions to the cluster’s world-class research programme in accelerator science. 

 The cluster’s work currently stretches over the following principal research areas:

 Scientific frontier facilities and underpinning technologies, including beam physics studies for particle colliders and light sources;

 Novel acceleration techniques, including beam and laser-driven acceleration, as well as micro accelerators;

 Applications of accelerators in addressing global challenges with a focus on medical applications and the commercialization of accelerator technologies.

 The scientific frontier facilities on which we aim to focus for the next decade include the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN; the Future Circular Collider (FCC); and the low energy antimatter facility AD/ELENA.

 We will continue to push the development of novel acceleration techniques. We are a key partner in the EuPRAXIA facility and involved in many international collaborations such as PACRI and EPITA where we combine cutting-edge R&D with leadership in cross-sector knowledge transfer. Our research focuses in particular on more sustainable accelerators, the development of high-resolution diagnostics and knowledge transfer with identified industry partners. 

 We also carry out research into high impact applications of accelerators to address global challenges in health, security, energy, manufacturing and the environment. The accelerator science cluster has led a number of European research and training networks in these areas and works closely with industry partners in the UK and around the world.

 Candidates are expected to develop the cluster’s cutting-edge research portfolio, work with our international partners, maximise the impact from our projects, co-supervise PhD and undergraduate students and contribute to research grant applications and the dissemination of our research results.

 We are looking for an outstanding accelerator scientist to make important contributions to the cluster’s research and training programme. Your research will involve leadership in one are several of the following areas: accelerator design and optimization, sustainable accelerator technologies including AI, novel acceleration techniques, sensor and beam instrumentation development, and accelerator applications.

 There are opportunities to contribute to teaching and supervision, and to make important contributions to major European projects such as High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), EuPRAXIA, EPITA and TwinRISE.

 This role is based at the Cockcroft Institute on the campus of Daresbury Laboratory. The research will be carried out at partner institutions around the world, and some national and international travel will be required.

 Candidates should have a PhD in a relevant discipline and an excellent track record in accelerator design and optimization, demonstrated through publications in high impact journals. Experience in the training and supervision of students will be an asset. The working language is English.

 Our commitment to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion  

 We are committed to enhancing a workforce as diverse as our community and particularly encourage applicants who are of minoritised genders and ethnic backgrounds, living with a disability, and/or are members of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Senior Research Associate in Hydroclimatic Extremes and Causal Pathways
Requisition ID:  29828
Location:  

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Fixed Term
Working Pattern:  Full Time
Posted Date:  13 Oct 2026

Salary: £48,337 to £51,258 per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 27 October 2026 

 

The Role

 

The EXTREME-FUTURES project will develop a seamless framework for predicting hydroclimatic extremes by connecting global climate drivers, regional weather regimes and extreme events across weather-to-climate timescales. The project focuses on persistent and connected extremes, including heatwaves, floods, storms and compound events, and will combine causal inference, feature tracking, observations and reanalysis, high-resolution modelling, and AI/machine learning.

 

As Senior Research Associate, you will lead key analyses within Work Package 1:Causal Pathways. You will identify extreme and compound temperature and precipitation events across multiple spatial and temporal scales; investigate the interactions between large-scale climate drivers, circulation regimes and atmospheric features that create pathways to extremes; and develop statistical and AI/ML approaches to identify semi-predictable pathways. The work will begin in Europe, using established weather-regime classifications and comprehensive observations, and will then expand globally. You will work closely with colleagues at ETH Zurich, the UK Met Office, ECMWF and the wider EXTREME-FUTURES team, contributing to WP1’s key outcome: a seamless framework for impactful hydroclimatic events from weather to climate scales.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles. These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

 

Newcastle University is committed to the responsible use of research metrics as part of our research culture and research strategy. We advocate for the transparent, appropriate, and inclusive use of metrics, guided by expert judgment, to support high-quality, impactful research that is open, collaborative and sustainable.

 

Contact for the post: Professor Hayley Fowler 

 

Duration of post: 24 months

 

To apply , please upload your CV along with covering letter that evidences how your skills and experience aligns to the person specification as outlined within the job description.

 

Key Accountabilities

Assess global temperature and precipitation anomalies across multiple temporal and spatial scales, relative to climatology, to identify extreme and compound hydroclimatic events.
Work with the wider project team to investigate causal pathways to European extreme events and subsequently extend the analysis globally, linking climate drivers, circulation/weather regimes and tracked atmospheric features.
Apply and develop robust statistical and causal-inference approaches to identify key driver–feature interactions and quantify relationships associated with persistent, connected and compound extremes.
Collaborate with project partners to develop and evaluate AI/ML algorithms that capture semi-predictable pathways to extreme events, and benchmark these against physical and machine-learning sub-seasonal to seasonal forecast systems.
Take a leading role in integrating, documenting and disseminating WP1 outputs, contributing to the project’s seamless weather-to-climate framework and to cross-work-package collaboration.
Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project.
Determine appropriate methodologies for research.
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations.
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations or through publications.
Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline.
Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding.

 

The Person

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

Knowledge and research experience in climate science, atmospheric science, meteorology, hydroclimatology, or a closely related quantitative discipline, with expertise relevant to weather and climate extremes.
Experience of analysing large observational, reanalysis, climate-model and/or weather-forecast datasets across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
Strong quantitative and scientific programming skills, for example in Python, R or an equivalent language, including reproducible data analysis and visualisation workflows.
Experience of statistical analysis relevant to climate variability and extremes; experience of causal inference, weather regimes/teleconnections, feature tracking, or compound-event analysis is highly desirable.
Experience of, or demonstrable ability to develop, AI/machine-learning methods for environmental or geophysical data.
Ability to collaborate effectively with methodological specialists.
Attention to detail and ability to work at high levels of accuracy
Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences

 - Human Genetics & Genomic Medicine

 Location:  Southampton General Hospital

 Full time fixed term until 31/08/2029 

 Interview date: To be confirmed

 The Faculty of Medicine Genomic Informatics Group invites applications for a full-time, fixed-term Senior Research Fellow position in AI Applied to Genomic Medicine. Based at the University Hospital Southampton site, you will work within a multidisciplinary team of genomic informaticians, clinicians and data scientists, leading translational research to improve genomic diagnostics for common autoimmune disease through advanced clinical and genomic data integration.

 As a Senior Research Fellow, you will:

 Lead a project to extract structured clinical findings from electronic health records (EHRs) using open-source large language models (LLMs) and harmonise findings to clinically relevant ontologies (in line with previously published research ).

 Drive translational research integrating clinical and genomic data to advance personalised diagnostics for common autoimmune disease.

 Develop, implement and maintain robust, reproducible LLM-based pipelines, using modern workflow systems and high‑performance computing platforms.

 Produce rigorous, high‑quality research outputs that advance applied genomic diagnostics and build your growing research profile.

 Contribute to the design and delivery of education and training in genomic data science for academic and clinical audiences.

 Effectively manage early career researchers in the planning and delivery of project objectives.

 Collaborate with local and international multidisciplinary colleagues across genomics, clinical medicine, data science, statistics, software engineering and compute infrastructure to deliver impactful research and project objectives.

 The successful candidate will work at the interface of University Genomic Informatic Research , high-performance compute infrastructure (IRIDIS) , NIHR Biomedical Research Centre , and the Southampton Emerging Therapies and Technologies (SETT) group .

 You will bring:

 A PhD in health informatics, bioinformatics, genomics, computational biology, data science, or a closely related field.

 Extensive experience integrating genomic data with structured clinical or phenotypic data, and familiarity with clinical ontologies such as HPO, SNOMED CT and ICD-10

 Extensive hands‑on experience with using open-source large language models, EHR data extraction, high‑throughput sequencing data analysis, and bioinformatics workflows used in research and/or diagnostic settings.

 Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, R, Perl, C/C++, Bash) and confidence working across Linux and other operating systems.

 Experience with ontology management software.

 Experience with data governance for handling sensitive EHR, genomic, and clinical data.

 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, enabling you to collaborate effectively across disciplines and convey complex concepts to diverse stakeholders.

 Proven ability to conduct research, work independently, and manage competing demands across projects.

 Proven ability to publish original research as a first author.

 At Southampton, you will be part of a world-class research environment with access to facilities, expertise and professional development opportunities. We can offer:

 Access to cutting‑edge technologies, high‑performance computing and secure data environments across academic and NHS settings.

 Opportunities to work with national partners such as NHS Genomic Medicine Service, Genomics England, Health Data Research Service secure data environments, Biomedical Research Centres and population‑scale datasets.

 A multidisciplinary research community with links across medicine, computational sciences, and translational research.

 Professional development, mentoring, and opportunities to build research independence.

 A supportive and inclusive working environment committed to equality and diversity, including Athena SWAN principles.

 A competitive benefits package, including generous holiday allowances, pension scheme membership, flexible and part‑time working options, and access to subsidised campus facilities.

 For informal enquiries, please contact S.Ennis@southampton.ac.uk .

Job Title: Research Fellow

Reference:  450             

Department: Physics

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 30 March 2028

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Tuesday 3 November 2026, 11:59pm (UK)                   

Full time Salary Range: £36,320.00 - £46,970.00 per annum

About the Role

The Semiconductor Research Group within the Department of Physics is seeking to appoint a Research Fellow in Group-IV Semiconductor Materials Science to undertake experimental research on advanced SiGe and Ge-based semiconductor heterostructures, with particular emphasis on the compressively strained germanium-on-silicon (cs-GoS) material platform.

 

The post will focus primarily on the structural, morphological, optical and electrical characterisation of Group-IV semiconductor materials and devices. The successful candidate will be expected to undertake substantial hands-on experimental work using techniques including transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), high-resolution X-ray diffraction (HR-XRD), X-ray reflectivity (XRR), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR); Hall-effect and resistivity measurements, and C–V and I–V characterisation from ~300 K down to ~300 mK .

 

The Research Fellow will work closely with colleagues involved in epitaxial growth, device fabrication and electrical transport measurements, and will be expected to correlate structural and materials properties with device performance. The role will include experimental planning, data analysis and interpretation, preparation of scientific publications, presentation of results, and contributions to externally funded collaborative research projects.

 

The appointment is initially offered on a 12-month fixed-term basis, with the possibility of extension subject to continued funding, project requirements and satisfactory performance.

 

The post is available for an early start following completion of the recruitment process and all required pre-employment checks.

 

Working Arrangements:

 

This is a laboratory-based, on-site position. The research requires extensive hands-on experimental work using specialist laboratories at the University of Warwick. The successful candidate will therefore be expected to work predominantly on site, Monday to Friday, during normal laboratory working hours, and to be routinely available during the working day to undertake experiments, use shared research facilities, collaborate with colleagues and deliver project activities. Candidates should expect to be normally present on site during the core working day, approximately 09:00–18:00, Monday to Friday, subject to contractual working arrangements and the requirements of the experimental programme. Regular remote or home working is not compatible with the core duties of this position. Limited flexibility for specific desk-based activities may be possible where appropriate, subject to operational requirements and University policy.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for an experimental materials scientist or semiconductor physicist with strong practical experience in the characterisation of Group-IV semiconductor materials, particularly SiGe and Ge-based heterostructures.

 

Applicants must be able to demonstrate substantial hands-on laboratory experience, rather than solely theoretical knowledge or indirect familiarity, in the structural and physical characterisation of semiconductor materials and devices.

 

Particular importance will be placed on practical experience and data interpretation using:

 

TEM and/or high-resolution TEM, including analysis of epitaxial layer structure, interfaces, defects and strain;
AFM, including quantitative surface morphology and roughness analysis;
HR-XRD, including analysis of composition, strain, relaxation, crystalline quality;
FTIR and related optical characterisation techniques.

 

Experience with SEM, XRR, Hall-effect and resistivity measurements, C–V and I–V characterisation will also be highly relevant.

 

Candidates should have a good understanding of epitaxial semiconductor heterostructures and be able to interpret experimental data quantitatively. Familiarity with SiGe epitaxy, CVD growth, semiconductor device processing and the cs-GoS material platform is highly essential.

 

The successful candidate will be expected to work both independently and collaboratively, plan experimental programmes, meet defined project milestones and deliverables, maintain high standards of laboratory practice and documentation, and communicate research findings effectively in publications, reports and presentations.

 

Due to the strongly experimental nature of the role, candidates must be prepared to work predominantly on site and to organise their working pattern around laboratory access, experimental schedules and project milestones.

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£35,302 per annum). Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£36,320 per annum).

About the Department

Semiconductor Research Group

 

For further information about the group, please visit our website at:

https://www.warwick.ac.uk/silicon

 

Department of Physics

 

The post will be based in the Department of Physics, a vibrant academic department with 200 academic, research, technical and professional services staff, over 800 undergraduate students and 200 postgraduate research students.

 

We are proud of our diverse community of staff, students, and visitors, and are committed to maintaining an excellent record in teaching and research by ensuring that there is equality of opportunity for all, fostered in an environment of mutual respect and dignity.

 

We hold an Athena SWAN Silver award, a national initiative to promote gender equality for all staff and students. We are also a Juno Champion, which is an award from the Institute of Physics to recognise our efforts to address the under-representation of women in university physics and to encourage better practice for both women and men. 

 

Further information about working in the Department of Physics and the benefits available can be found at www.warwick.ac.uk/physics/staff/working/.

 

The University supports flexible working and requests for part-time working or job-share will be considered where possible.

 

Childcare for interviews

 

Childcare can be provided for you at the University of Warwick Nursery (www.warwick.ac.uk/services/childrensservices/nursery) in order for you to attend the interview. Childcare is subject to availability of places at the Nursery.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. 

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held in mid-November.

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.

 Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine

 Contract: Full time, FTC for 12 months 

 We are recruiting a curious, rigorous and delivery-minded scientist to help turn the complexity of vaccine design into a usable decision platform. Malaria remains one of the world’s most important infectious diseases, but the search space for new peptide-based vaccines is enormous. A single parasite proteome can generate millions of possible peptides, and the strongest candidates must satisfy multiple constraints simultaneously

 You will join an interdisciplinary malaria research programme at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine and work within the MalariaGEN team, collaborating with international vaccine researchers and making use of large-scale computational resources. The initial focus will be T-cell antigen and peptide prioritisation, with opportunities to contribute to broader computational antigen discovery as the programme develops.

 You can learn more about this opportunity by reading our blog post about the project, as well as exploring some of our previous work in this area. 

 In this role, you will have the opportunity to: 

 Build the core decision platform at scale. Develop scalable, tested and documented local and cloud workflows for malaria peptide evaluation, MHC class I and II predictions, multi-omics integration, ranking and candidate-set optimisation across very large datasets.

 Integrate evidence and improve prediction. Combine antigen-presentation methods with HLA population coverage, parasite variation, conservation, expression, and other evidence layers while calibrating predictions with experimental data and quantifying model uncertainty and disagreement. 

 Turn data and experiments into decisions. Develop transparent scoring, filtering and optimisation approaches that help collaborators compare candidates and design experimentally tractable peptide sets; ingest assay results, assess prediction performance and iteratively improve prioritisation methods.

 Collaborate and create reusable research outputs. Work with international collaborators to provide analyses, technical support and help with scientific interpretation, while producing reusable pipelines, structured datasets and databases, technical documentation, scientific reports, presentations and peer-reviewed publications.

 The successful candidate will have: 

 A PhD in a relevant quantitative or life-science discipline, or equivalent substantial experience delivering advanced computational research or data-science projects.

 Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, together with sound software-engineering practices.

 Experience analysing or managing large, complex biological, biomedical or similarly high-dimensional datasets.

 Experience with statistical analysis, machine learning, quantitative method development and model evaluation.

 Experience building reproducible workflows and analytical pipelines, ideally using HPC or cloud computing environments.

 (For a full list of essential and desirable criteria please refer to the job description and person specification) 

 Application Process:  To apply for this position please follow the apply link and upload your CV, complete our application form and attach a covering letter outlining your interest in the post, and how your skills and experience align.

Senior Research Associate in Vegetation and Fire Modelling
 Apply
The role

The Postdoctoral Research Associate will work on the Copernicus Fire and Land-Atmosphere Modelling of Emissions (CoFLAME) project. CoFLAME will deliver scientific and technical advances to better account for interactions between wildfires and vegetation, improving estimates of wildfire emissions and natural CO₂ fluxes, while enhancing the forecasting of fire activity, fire probability, and fire spread.

At the University of Bristol, you will develop new theoretical and modelling frameworks to quantify vegetation recovery, mortality, and ecosystem legacy effects following fire. This work will combine data synthesis, model development, and analysis to deliver new process-orientated insights into post-fire ecosystem dynamics and the role of vegetation legacies in shaping land-atmosphere carbon exchange and ecosystem resilience under future climate change.

You will join the research lab of Professor Martin De Kauwe at the University of Bristol and will collaborate closely with an international team of researchers within the Copernicus Fire and Land-Atmosphere Modelling of Emissions (CoFLAME) project. Coordinated by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), the consortium brings together leading scientists from the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI), GEOVILLE, NILU (Norway), the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute (KNMI), and the Portuguese Institute for Sea and Atmosphere (IPMA).

Hybrid working is available and can be discussed at interview.  This is a full-time (100%) position but appointment at 80% time would be considered.

What will you be doing?

You will contribute to the Copernicus Fire and Land-Atmosphere Modelling of Emissions (CoFLAME) project by developing and applying new approaches to represent how vegetation responds to and recovers from wildfire. Working at the interface of ecosystem science, Earth system modelling, and remote sensing, you will investigate the impacts of fire on vegetation structure, carbon cycling, and ecosystem recovery. The role will involve developing and testing new model representations of post-fire vegetation dynamics, analysing observational and satellite datasets, and collaborating with international partners to improve the representation of fire-vegetation interactions in next-generation land surface models and forecasting systems.

You should apply if

You have:

A PhD (or soon to be awarded) in mathematics, vegetation modelling, physics, atmospheric science, or similar quantitative discipline.
Significant experience in ecosystem, vegetation, land surface, or Earth system modelling, ideally with applications to wildfire, disturbance, or ecosystem recovery.
Demonstrated programming/computing skills in a Unix/Linux environment.
Strong research and publication track record (relative to career opportunity)
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team and independently in a research environment.

Additional information

Contract type: Open-ended (fixed funding for 3 years)

Work pattern: Full-time (100%) position but appointment at 80% time would be considered.

Grade: J

Salary: £44,746 - £50,253 per annum

School/Unit: Biological Sciences

This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on Thursday 5th November 2026

For informal queries please contact: Professor Martin De Kauwe, Professor of Global Change Ecology via email: m.dekauwe@bristol.ac.uk

Interviews will be held during week commencing 16th November 2026

postings.advert_text:
A position exists for a Research Assistant in the Department of Engineering, to work on mechanics of fusion materials. The post holder will be located in Central Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, UK.

We are starting a new research project focused on developing damage-tolerant materials for space and fusion-energy applications with an emphasis on refractory, body-centered cubic alloys, and high stacking fault energy alloys. Materials used in space and fusion systems must retain their structural integrity under extreme combinations of mechanical loading, temperature, and irradiation. These materials are often very brittle, but new processing techniques, including but not limited to additive manufacturing, can potentially mitigate this issue. The project will investigate the fundamental mechanisms that govern deformation and damage in these materials and use this understanding to identify new approaches to their design. The role holder will conduct experimental research to characterise how candidate materials deform plastically (if at all) and resist fracture.

The work will involve performing mechanical characterisation including tensile, toughness and fatigue testing at room and elevated temperatures, performing electron microscopy characterisation including electron backscatter diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, and analysing/interpreting the resulting data. The candidate will be familiar with ASTM E399, E1820, and E647, dislocation mechanics, and microscopy techniques. The job will also include developing equipment including a micronotcher, vacuum-furnace and cryogenic testing system. The findings will be used to establish a first principles understanding and for the development of materials with improved resistance to damage and neutron irradiation.

The role holder will work closely with other members of the research group at Cambridge and with external collaborators, including at Lawrence Livermore National Labs. They will be expected to contribute to group meetings, present their findings, prepare research publications, and assist with grant administration.

The skills, qualifications and experience required to perform the roles are wide. The specific skills include excellent laboratory skills and data analysis capabilities.

The applicant is expected to have at least a Bachelor's degree in Engineering Science or Materials Science and Engineering. A Master's degree is preferable.

Salary Range:

£33,662 - £36,320

Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 4 months in the first instance.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Please ensure that you upload your Curriculum Vitae (CV), a covering letter and publication list in the Upload section of the online application. If you upload any additional documents which have not been requested, we will not be able to consider these as part of your application. Please submit your application by midnight on the closing date.

If you have any questions about this vacancy or the application process, please contact Dr David Cook by email at dhc40@cam.ac.uk.

Please quote reference NM51485 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

postings.title: Research Software Engineer (Part Time, Fixed Term)
postings.listing_context: Research Software Engineer (Part Time, Fixed Term) Institute of Astronomy £35,608-£46,049 pro rata Professional services 22 September 2026 9 November 2026 LG50949
postings.advert_text:
Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 5 years in the first instance. If additional funding is acquired, extension may be possible.

The Institute of Astronomy (IoA) and the co-located, interdepartmental Kavli Institute for Cosmology, Cambridge (KICC) at Cambridge University are internationally renowned for a uniquely stimulating and multi-disciplinary research environment. One topic where Cambridge has a long history is black holes, the most extreme environments in nature, and laboratories where strong gravity, plasma physics and high-energy astro(particle)/physical processes meet. The research group of Prof. Sera Markoff (Plumian Professor) studies these systems across the full black hole mass scale, combining GPU-accelerated supercomputer simulations and semi-analytic modelling with data from world-leading facilities including the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT). Her group sits at the nexus of several international efforts: a growing Cambridge node, where this post is based (currently expanding over the coming years into a fully-fledged team of students and postdocs); an established group at the University of Amsterdam of several postdocs and students; her ongoing ERC Synergy Grant project 'Blackholistic', with partner groups at Oxford, Radboud University in Nijmegen, the University of Turku, the University of Namibia and the University of South Africa; and major international collaborations including the EHT and the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Via the ERC project, the group is also involved in commissioning a new 14-metre radio telescope in Namibia, the Africa Millimetre Telescope.

The group's research is built on a developing portfolio of in-house software: a GPU-accelerated general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulation code (in C, with GPU acceleration primarily on NVIDIA and AMD hardware); a GR ray-tracing code (in Julia) that produces images and spectra from those simulations, and is designed to conduct Bayesian parameter inference; semi-analytic jet and accretion modelling codes (in C++, with a Python interface) that are being integrated into the open-source Gammapy framework for use across the CTAO community and beyond; and increasingly building on other imaging and analysis frameworks used within the EHT Collaboration. These codes run on local, national and international high-performance computing (HPC) facilities.

This part-time 0.5 FTE Research Software Engineer (RSE) role will provide the professional software engineering capability at the centre of this network and will suit someone excited to work at the interface between modern software engineering and some of the most cutting-edge research in astrophysics.

The role-holder will establish and manage version-controlled repositories for all group software, deploy and optimise the codes on available HPC facilities, and embed good software practice across a distributed, international team through documentation, testing, code review and training. The role has a strong outward-facing dimension: coordinating shared code development with partner institutions and contributing the group's codes to community open-source frameworks used by international collaborations.

The purpose of the role is to ensure that the group's research software is reliable, performant, well-documented and reproducible; that development remains coordinated with partner groups as shared codes evolve; and that software engineering expertise is retained within the group as projects and personnel change. The role also offers clear scope for growth: the role-holder will be encouraged to engage directly in the group's research, helping develop new computational methods and contributing to publications, with responsibilities that can expand as the Cambridge node grows.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

In particular, the role-holder's responsibilities will include:

Establishing and managing reliable version-control infrastructure for the group's codes, including migration of legacy repositories. Defining repository structure, branching, access and release workflows so that all group software is secure, documented, citable and reproducible.

Liaising with partner development groups at other institutions to track external development branches of shared codes. Planning and carrying out the integration of selected external developments into the group's versions, coordinating builds and testing.

Setting up, testing and optimising the group's numerical simulation codes on local, national and international (US/CAN/EU) HPC clusters using AMD and/or NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., via CUDA, HIP, OpenCL, or similar). Carrying out application profiling and benchmarking, and contributing technical cases and support to group proposals for acquiring more HPC computing time.

Designing, coding, verifying, testing and documenting new physics capabilities within the group's codes, together with the research team, profiling and optimising their performance.

Investigating, prototyping and implementing machine-learning and advanced statistical methods (e.g. improved sampling for Bayesian parameter inference, surrogate models/emulators, simulation-based inference) to accelerate the group's modelling and inference workflows; evaluating their performance and implements improvements.

Supporting development of the group's semi-analytic modelling codes (C++ with a Python interface) through performance optimisation and branch management, and planning and carrying out their integration into the open-source Gammapy framework, adhering to community coding standards, so that they can be adopted across the CTAO community and beyond.

Implementing automated testing, continuous integration and documentation across the group's codebases. Providing advice, guidance and training to researchers and students in both Cambridge and Amsterdam to promote adoption of software engineering best practice.

Actively maintaining specialist knowledge and providing detailed advice to group leader Prof. Markoff on software strategy, computing resource planning and data-management plans for grant proposals and reports.

Within the group's research goals, building on and refining ideas for developing and evaluating new computational methods, collaborating with researchers on their application to open problems; reporting on work carried out and potentially contributing material of publication quality to group publications.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Please indicate the contact details of three professional referees on the online application form and upload a full curriculum vitae (CV), list of publications (if you have such) and a research/technical experience statement (this research/technical experience statement being three pages max in 11pt font).

The closing date for applications is: 23:59 BST on Monday 9th November 2026.

Referees will be requested to provide references by the same date. Where permission is given by the applicant, references will be requested prior to the vacancy closing. Applicants are asked to inform their referees that they will receive a reference request communication including a link to upload a reference to the University of Cambridge recruitment system by the application closing date.

Applications will be reviewed after the closing date and interviews are provisionally planned for: w/c 30th November 2026.

We anticipate that this 0.5 FTE post is equivalent to circa 18.5 hours per week, flexibility in exact working hours per week may be required. As a guide, the General Board expects the average full-time working week for academic-related employees to be in the region of 37 to 40 hours, therefore a part-time, 0.5 working week can be considered on average to be 18.5 to 20 hours per week.

For any queries regarding the application please contact: hr@ast.cam.ac.uk. Informal enquiries may be addressed to Professor Sera Markoff via her EA, Joanna Carruthers, at plumianprofea@ast.cam.ac.uk.

Please quote reference LG50949 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

The University of Cambridge is a signatory to the San-Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA), and in recruitment or promotion evaluations will assess research on the basis of its merits rather than the journal or venue in which it is published. Applicants should not include Journal Impact Factors or uncontextualized metrics in their applications. Full details are at: https://www.research-strategy.admin.cam.ac.uk/research-policy/DORA

Working at Durham University  

A globally outstanding centre of teaching and research excellence, a warm and friendly place to work, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.

As one of the UK’s leading universities, Durham is an incredible place to define your career. The University is located within a beautiful historic city, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and surrounded by stunning countryside. Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University, it’s also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page

The Role and Department
A World Top 100 department in the 2025 QS subject rankings, our research spans advanced instrumentation, astronomy and astrophysics, condensed matter physics, cosmology, particle physics and quantum physics. It has real‑world impact, informing developments in energy storage, improved cancer imaging, quantum computing, nuclear fusion, pandemic modelling and faster digital technologies. We pride ourselves on closely aligning our teaching with the University’s research‑intensive ethos. Research‑led learning is embedded at every stage of our undergraduate programmes—from first‑year laboratory reports to our flagship final‑year MPhys individual research projects—ensuring our students develop the skills and insight needed for future roles in STEM.

The successful candidate will join the Quantum Light and Matter (QLM) research section, a vibrant community working on the forefront of quantum science and technology, with experimental activities spanning cold atoms and molecules, thermal vapours and solid-state systems. Complementary theory activities and excellent technical support, together with an strong national and international network provide the ideal environment for cutting-edge experimental quantum science and technology.   

The Role

We are recruiting a Postdoctoral Research Associate on the project ‘Quantum networking at telecom wavelengths with Yb qubits’. The research project is funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) and led by EPSRC Quantum Technology fellow Dr Tobias Franzen. The project aims to develop a key technology for future quantum networks by combining arrays of single Yb atoms as a leading qubit platform with long-distance quantum networking over existing telecom fibre infrastructure. Possible applications include the scaling of neutral-atom quantum computing through distributed computing, as well as new tests of fundamental physics, such as exploring the interplay of general relativity and quantum mechanics through experiments with entangled clocks separated in space.

To realise this vision, we are working on a modular ytterbium tweezer-array platform, compact laser setups, and cavity-enhanced atom-photon interfaces for efficient remote entanglement generation over telecom-wavelength optical fibre links.

We are seeking an ambitious and highly motivated researcher with a background in AMO physics, quantum optics, or related fields. The successful applicant will work closely with Dr Tobias Franzen to realise the projects goals. They will be expected to take an active role in all aspects of the project, contributing directly to the experiment and working with national and international collaborators, undergraduate and graduate students, other members of the research group and technical staff.

The post holder will be expected to display the initiative, creativity, skills and knowledge required to advance the project. They need to work effectively both independently and as part of a small research team to solve technical and scientific challenges. It is expected that the successful applicant will enhance the international contacts of the group through the presentation of work at international conferences. The post holder will also be expected to aid in the supervision of graduate students within the group as well as contributing to the undergraduate teaching within the Department.

The postdoctoral researcher will have opportunities to develop scientific leadership, build international collaborations, contribute to grant proposals and supervise students.

Key responsibilities:

To understand and convey material of a specialist or highly technical nature to the team or group of people through presentations and discussions that leads to the presentation of research papers in conferences and publications.

To prepare and deliver presentations on research outputs/activities to audiences which may include: research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To publish high quality outputs, including papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and papers for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To assist with the development of research objectives and proposals.
To conduct individual and collaborative research projects under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To work with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify areas for research, develop new research methods and extend the research portfolio.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines by discussing with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and offering creative or innovative solutions.
To liaise with research colleagues and make internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to form relationships for future research collaboration.
To plan and manage own research activity, research resources in collaboration with others and contribute to the planning of research projects.
To deliver training in research techniques/approaches to peers, visitors and students as appropriate.
To be involved in student supervision, as appropriate, and assist with the assessment of the knowledge of students.
To contribute to fostering a collegial and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.

To engage in continuing professional development by participation in the undergraduate or postgraduate teaching programmes or by membership of departmental committees, etc. and by attending relevant training and development courses.   

 

The appointment will initially be made for 24 months, with the possibility for extension subject to performance and funding availability.

The post-holder is employed to work on research/a research project which will be led by another colleague. Whilst this means that the post-holder will not be carrying out independent research in his/her own right, the expectation is that they will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of their own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

The starting date is flexible, with the successful candidate ideally being in post by April 2027.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University:

You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. The University closes between Christmas and New Year.

We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key component of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our Purpose and Values and our Staff Code of Conduct.  At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive.

We welcome and encourage applications from those who are currently under-represented in our work force, including people with disabilities and from racially minoritised ethnic groups.

The selection committee will take this into account when evaluating your application.

The University has been awarded the Disability Confident Leader status. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role.

If you encounter technical difficulties when using the online application form, we prefer you send enquiries by email.  Please send your name along with a brief description of the problem you’re experiencing to e.recruitment@durham.ac.uk 

Alternatively, you may call 0191 334 6801 from the UK, or +44 191 334 6801 from outside the UK. This number operates during the hours of 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday, UK time.  We will normally respond within one working day (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays).

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification below. While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.

Short-listed candidates will be invited to the University, either virtually or in-person and will have the opportunity to meet key members of the Department.  The assessment for the post will normally include a short presentation followed by an interview and we anticipate that the interviews will take place in or around November 2026. 

In the event that you are unable to attend in person on the date offered, it may not be possible to offer you an interview on an alternative date. 

Please note that in submitting your application Durham University will be processing your data. Research Associate in Prospective Life Cycle Assessment of Tyre Recycling Processes
Edinburgh, Midlothian, United Kingdom

Role Title:
 Research Associate in Prospective Life Cycle Assessment of Tyre Recycling Processes

Grade and Salary: 

Grade 7, £38,448 - £48,337 per annum

FTE and working pattern: 

Full-time (35hrs per week) Fixed Term (24 Months)

Reward and Benefits
:
 

33 days annual leave, plus 9 buildings closed days for all full time staff. Use our total rewards calculator:
 

https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm

 
to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University. 

Purpose of Role 

The 
Research Centre for Carbon Solutions
 are recruiting a postdoctoral research associate to work on the design and prospective life cycle analysis of novel rubber tyre recycling processes. This is an exciting role for very high-performing environmental life cycle researchers that wish to work on the complexities of predicting the future environmental footprint of very early-stage tyre recycling processes. 

The role is part of the EPSRC sponsored tyre to tyre project, where Heriot Watt develops new technology to go from used rubber tyre crumbs straight to new solid tyre precursors. We do this via mechanochemical functionalisation of the used rubber crumb, that activates the used rubber and prepares it to feed straight into tyre manufacturing processes. The project is highly interdisciplinary, and includes chemistry and reactor design and testing, process design and life cycle environmental impact evaluation, process upscaling, and innovation, market, and policy analysis. We work with many industrial partners, including recycling and waste collection companies and multinational tyre manufacturers.

The postholder will develop and optimise process designs for the new tyre recycling process, and evaluate different designs using life cycle environmental performance principles. This involves chemical engineering process design (taking inputs from the reactor design and from the upscaling studies) and life cycle assessment. A key element of the work involves the prospective life cycle assessment, that aims to investigate the environmental performance of different process designs in selected future scenarios, including net-zero scenarios – in line with EPSRC’s ambitions towards achieving the UK governments net-zero goals. 

The Research Centre for Carbon Solutions offers a very ambitious yet pleasant and collegial working environment. We strive to set the standards in technology development, scale up, and evaluation, instead of following existing practices. We have and offer strong exposure to relevant research, industry, and policy communities, providing a good springboard for early career researchers desiring to kickstart their scientific career. 

Person Specification 

These are the criteria on which the short-listing and recruitment selection will be made.

The ideal candidate has a first degree in chemical, process, or environmental engineering or similar, and a PhD (or soon to finalise their PhD or substantial professional experience) with a strong LCA element. You will have worked on evaluating emerging technologies for decarbonisation or circular economies. A good command of typical LCA software (e.g., SimaPro, Gabi) is expected, with good command of research level LCA software (Brightway) beneficial. Furthermore, very strong analytical and conceptual skills are expected, as well as leadership in research design and delivery. 

Essential

A first degree in chemical, process, environmental engineering or similar

A (near) complete PhD or substantial work experience with a strong LCA component

Experience working on evaluation of early stage/emerging decarbonisation and/or recycling technologies

Proven leadership in research design and execution

Evidence of successfully working in interdisciplinary teams

Good command of commercial LCA software, e.g., Simapro, Gabi

A strong publication record commensurate to career level

Desirable

Experience with research level LCA software (Brightway)

Experience with prospective LCA (e.g., Premise)

Experience with programming/coding, or desire to develop this

Experience with computer aided process design (e.g., Aspen Plus, Hysys)

Strong communication and project management skills

How to Apply

Please submit via the Heriot-Watt on-line recruitment system (1) Cover letter describing your interest and suitability for the post; (2) Full CV

Applications can be submitted until 
23:55 on Tuesday 10
th
 November 2026.

We may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application promptly.

About the role

Build the Next Generation of Health Policy Simulation Models

Do you want your research to influence how governments design policies to prevent chronic disease? Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems?

The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience.

Why This Role Matters

Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. Health-GPS provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes.

Health-GPS represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time.

You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including:

GOLDFINCH – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption.
JA Prevent NCD – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention.
JACARDI – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk.

Working with economists, epidemiologists, and data scientists, you’ll push the boundaries of policy simulation and shape real-world decision-making.

This is a hands-on computational role. Alongside using Health-GPS for policy analysis, you will write, test and review code in its C++ codebase, working within the team’s collaborative development workflow (version control, pull requests and code review). C++ experience is highly desirable, but we also welcome strong programmers in other relevant languages who are willing to work in C++.

What you would be doing

Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance.
Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time.
Help integrate new methodologies, including AI and machine-learning approaches, into simulation design.
Conduct quantitative analyses to estimate the health and economic impact of proposed policies.
Identify and manage relevant datasets in collaboration with internal and external partners.
Communicate findings through academic papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder workshops.
Contribute to funding proposals and the expansion of CHEPI’s modelling activities.

What we are looking for

We’re seeking a creative and technically strong individual with:

A PhD (or equivalent, or near completion) in health economics, epidemiology, computer science, or a related field.
Experience building or using microsimulation models or other quantitative policy tools.
Strong programming skills in at least one language (e.g. Python, R, or C++), and experience contributing to a shared codebase using version control (e.g. git).
Experience working with large or longitudinal datasets.
The ability to translate complex model outputs into actionable policy insights.
Curiosity, independence, and enthusiasm for multidisciplinary collaboration.

Experience with C++ is highly desirable. Experience applying AI or ML methods to health or policy modelling is also desirable.

Candidates for appointment as Research Fellow should also demonstrate a strong publication record, experience contributing to funding proposals, and the ability to design and lead original research.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Interested? Apply online with:

A cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant experience, and indicating the level (Research Associate or Research Fellow) for which you are applying.
Your CV.
Contact details for two referees.

This position is full-time and fixed-term for 24 months, with potential for extension depending on funding. Start date: as soon as possible.

For queries about the post, contact Prof. Franco Sassi (f.sassi@imperial.ac.uk).

About the role

Could your expertise in computational modelling, neutronics or AI methods help design and manage the nuclear reactors of tomorrow as a Research Associate in Applied Nuclear Computation? Working within Imperial College London's world-leading Applied Modelling & Computation Group (AMCG), you will apply advanced numerical, physics-based and data-driven methods to one or two exciting and complementary projects: an industry-funded digital engineering platform focused on the design and optimisation of a novel thorium reactor, and a UKRI-backed agentic digital ecosystem supporting the full lifecycle of next-generation High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactors (HTGRs).

What you would be doing

As a Research Associate in the AMCG, you will contribute to internationally leading research, taking the initiative in planning and executing your own scientific work to contribute to the broader goals of two cutting-edge nuclear projects.

You will develop and apply advanced computational, numerical and physics-based methods, ensuring the validity and reliability of your data and maintaining meticulous records of your findings throughout. Your work will span the full research cycle — from identifying and developing appropriate techniques for data collection and analysis, to writing reports for research sponsors, submitting publications to high-quality refereed journals, and presenting your findings at national and international conferences.

You will also have the opportunity to lead and mentor, directing small research teams and providing guidance to PhD students and research assistants, helping to shape the next generation of computational scientists.

Collaboration will be at the heart of your role, as you build and maintain relationships with allied researchers both within Imperial College and across the wider international community, contributing to grant bids and actively participating in group meetings and seminars. In everything you do, you will be expected to uphold the highest standards of research integrity, safety and professionalism, promoting the reputation of the AMCG, the Department and Imperial College London as a whole.

What we are looking for

With up to three posts available, we welcome applicants from a broad range of disciplines — including applied mathematical modelling, computational mathematics, reactor physics and AI — who are eager to bring their technical expertise to one of the most important clean energy challenges of our time. In particular, you will have:

 

A strong computational and numerical foundation — you hold a PhD (or have equivalent experience) in Applied Mathematics, Physics, Nuclear Engineering or a closely related computational discipline, and have hands-on experience developing software implementing discretisation methods such as Finite Element or Finite Volume approaches. (Note: Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.)
Scientific programming proficiency — you are confident writing and deploying scientific code in one or more of Fortran, C/C++ or Python, ideally with experience developing and running codes in High Performance Computing (HPC) environments.
Familiarity with reactor physics methods and tools — experience with neutronics, fuel cycle or burnup/depletion modelling — whether through codes such as OpenMC, Serpent, MCNP, WIMS or SCALE, or through knowledge of advanced reactor concepts such as HTGRs or thorium systems — is highly advantageous, though not essential.
An interest in or exposure to AI and data-driven modelling — experience applying machine learning or reduced-order modelling techniques to physics problems, such as training neural networks on simulation data, would be a valuable addition to our multidisciplinary team.
A track record of research delivery and communication — you can demonstrate experience working in a research environment, with the ability to write clearly for publication, present confidently at conferences, and engage effectively with both academic collaborators and industry partners.
A proactive, collaborative and organised approach to work — you are able to manage your own research programme with appropriate supervision, prioritise effectively against deadlines, and contribute positively to a team environment, including supporting and motivating junior researchers and students.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

This is a fixed term post for up to 33 months.

About the role

Are you a robot learning researcher eager to push the boundaries of dexterous manipulation? Join DexLab at Imperial College London, led by Dr. Rolandos Potamias and Stefanos Zafeiriou, in a postdoctoral research role to lead transformative projects spanning robot foundation models and real-world dexterous manipulation. 

DexLab at Imperial is seeking a highly motivated and talented Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA / PostDoc) who has demonstrated competence in conducting cutting-edge robot learning research. The position focuses on building dexterous, high-degree-of-freedom (high-DoF) manipulation policies and robot foundation models, such as vision-language-action models (VLAs), learned from human demonstrations, but is not limited to this. The successful candidate will work on a state-of-the-art robotic platform comprising Sharpa Wave dexterous hands and UR7e arms, contributing both to methodological advances and to the deployment of learned policies on real robots. To this end, the role integrates knowledge from robot learning, computer vision, generative modelling and control. 

What you would be doing

The post will focus on research topics in probabilistic programming. The specific details of the project are flexible and will be determined based on the interests and strengths of the successful candidate.  

You will conduct original research at the intersection of dexterous manipulation, robot learning and foundation models, exploring how large-scale human demonstration data (e.g., video, motion capture and teleoperation) can be turned into capable, general-purpose robot behaviour. In particular, you will develop novel algorithms and policies for high-DoF hands and validate them on real hardware. In doing so, you will collaborate with a team of expert researchers in robotics, computer vision and machine learning. We strive to publish in top-tier conferences such as CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR, ECCV, ICCV, ICRA and RSS.  

What we are looking for

 

A strong track record in top conferences and journals in robot learning, machine learning or computer vision such as CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR, ECCV, ICCV, ICRA and RSS.
Demonstrated robot learning experience (e.g., imitation learning, learning from demonstrations, VLAs / robot foundation models, or reinforcement learning) is a must.
Strong PyTorch programming skills and working knowledge of ROS are a must. 
Hands-on experience deploying learned policies on real robots is a must; experience with dexterous hands, teleoperation or motion capture for demonstration collection is a plus. 
Applicants must hold a PhD in computer science, robotics, engineering or equivalent. 

You should have proven research record and publications in the relevant areas.  

Please see job description for a full list of requirements. 

What we can offer you

The chance to work in an exciting and rapidly developing area, with access to state-of-the-art hardware including Sharpa Wave hands and UR7e arms. This is a chance to grow and establish yourself as a leader in this field.
Dedicated mentorship as well as the freedom to explore your own ideas. 
Working closely with a team of PhD students and postdocs from different backgrounds. 
The Department of Computing is the top-1 ranked computer science department in the UK, according to REF 2021.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year). 
Disseminating your research in major robotics, machine learning and computer vision conferences is supported and travel costs will be covered. 

Further information

Full-time, fixed term position for 12 months to start as soon as possible

*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. 

In addition to completing the online application candidates should attach:

A full CV with a list of all publications
A research statement indicating what you see are interesting research issues relating to the above post and why your expertise is relevant

Informal enquiries related to the position should be directed to Dr Rolandos Potamias r.potamias19@imperial.ac.uk

For queries regarding the application process contact Jamie Perrins: j.perrins@imperial.ac.uk

About the role

We invite applications for a Research Associate to develop novel methods for pathogen genomic epidemiology in the Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology, School of Public Health, Faculty of Medicine, Imperial College London.

The post is funded by a Wellcome Early-Career Award and will be based in a new group within the Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology. The group develops scalable mathematical and statistical approaches leveraging large pathogen genome datasets to understand the determinants of infectious disease transmission. Our work combines data analysis, genomic epidemiology, mathematical modelling and statistical inference to answer public health relevant questions. We are committed to building a positive and inclusive environment, where all team members feel that they belong and are excited to do research. We recognise the systemic barriers that exist in higher education and research, particularly for people from historically marginalised groups. Applicants from groups underrepresented in science and research are particularly encouraged to apply.

What you would be doing

The successful candidate will develop and apply statistical and computational methods to characterise infectious disease transmission from pathogen genomic data, with an initial focus on seasonal influenza and opportunities to extend the work to other pathogens. Projects will build on approaches developed in the group that rely on genetically proximal sequences and do not require full phylogenetic tree reconstruction. The work will include a combination of method development and validation, computational simulations and data analysis, which can be balanced depending on the postholder’s interests and experience. This work is fundamentally interdisciplinary, combining infectious disease epidemiology, pathogen evolution, genomic epidemiology, mathematical modelling, statistical inference and quantitative data analysis.

We do not expect candidates to be experts in all these areas, and welcome applicants with a strong foundation in one or more relevant disciplines who are enthusiastic about developing expertise across these areas.

What we are looking for

Hold a PhD in infectious disease epidemiology, computational biology, population biology, biostatistics or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience *Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.
Demonstrated experience developing mathematical and/or statistical approaches to answer complex biological questions.
Experience conducting quantitative analyses of complex biological data using rigorous analytical approaches.
Experience disseminating research through high-quality scientific outputs, such as peer-reviewed publications, preprints, software tools and conference presentations.
Advanced programming skills in R and/or Python.
Knowledge of, or strong interest in learning about, infectious disease epidemiology.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant.

This is a full-time and fixed-term contract for two years. The expected start date for this post is 01st February 2027 (with flexibility on the start date), and the contract end date will be 31st January 2029.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr Cecile Tran Kiem – cecile.tran-kiem18@imperial.ac.uk.
