About us

King’s College London is one of the world's leading universities, ranked 31st globally and 5th in the UK in the QS World University Rankings 2026. Founded in 1829, King’s is a Russell Group university with a world-renowned reputation for excellence in education, research and innovation, particularly across medicine, health and the life sciences.

This post will be based within the newly established Department of Primary Care & Data Science, an interdisciplinary department that brings together expertise in primary care, population health, health informatics, artificial intelligence, epidemiology, biostatistics and health services research. The Department aims to develop innovative data-driven approaches to improve health and healthcare, working closely with patients, communities, policy-makers, healthcare providers and international partners.

The Department sits within the  School of Life Course & Population Health Sciences , one of six Schools that make up the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine at King’s College London. The School unites over 500 experts in a wide range of population health sciences including women and children’s health, life course sciences, nutritional sciences, Health AI, preventive medicine and the molecular genetics of human disease. Our research links the causes of common health problems to life’s landmark stages, treating life, disease and healthcare as a continuum. We are interdisciplinary by nature and this innovative approach works: 91 per cent of our research submitted to the Subjects Allied to Medicine (Pharmacy, Nutritional Sciences and Women's Health cluster) for REF was rated as world-leading or internationally excellent. We use this expertise to teach the next generation of health professionals and research scientists. Based across King’s Denmark Hill, Guy’s, St Thomas’ and Waterloo campuses, our academic programme of teaching, research and clinical practice is embedded across seven Departments.

About the role

We are seeking a post-doctoral health data scientist with a strong mix of Python scientific coding skills and applied health research expertise, to work on the METIUS AI work package (metiusevidence.org), which is co-led by King’s and UCL. The successful candidate will design, build and adapt AI-enabled evidence synthesis tools, help METIUS consortium partner organisations onboard and use them, and contribute to methodological and evaluation research.

METIUS (Mobilising Evidence Through Artificial Intelligence and User-Informed Synthesis) is an £11.5m UKRI-funded programme, led by Queen’s University Belfast, building breakthrough AI and open data infrastructure for rapid, living evidence synthesis. The consortium brings together 19 organisations, including King’s, to deliver exemplar syntheses across education, crime & justice, climate, and sustainable development, and to engage directly with policymakers.

You will design, build, and evaluate AI-enabled evidence synthesis tools and pipelines, writing well-documented, production-quality code, and will work directly with partner organisations across the consortium to configure and onboard these tools to their needs. You will design and run methodological and evaluation studies assessing the performance, reliability and usability of AI-assisted evidence synthesis methods, and write these up for publication.

You will work in a team with software developers, data scientists, and evidence synthesis specialists. Alongside METIUS, you will contribute to the related Solace-AI project (solaceai.org), applying AI-driven evidence synthesis methods to climate-health emergencies, and will develop new methods for making sure AI systems are trustworthy.

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 2 years from your start date.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria:

PhD awarded in Health Data Science, Computer Science, Epidemiology, Public Health, or a related quantitative field; or PhD in one of these subjects near completion.
Experience conducting high-quality evidence synthesis (including systematic reviews, and scoping, rapid, umbrella reviews, and guidelines) using formal methodological approaches (e.g. narrative synthesis, evidence mapping).
Strong software development skills; experienced in version control/GitHub; expertise in using Python scientific stack (jupyter/numpy/scipy/sci-kit learn/pandas etc).
Strong publication track record as demonstrated through first-author publications in peer-reviewed journals.
Demonstrated ability to design and conduct applied health or policy research studies, including study design, quantitative analysis, and interpretation of findings.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable criteria:

Experience in stakeholder engagement: working with policy makers, humanitarian organisations, international partners, and/or the public.
Experience contributing to multi-partner or consortium research projects, e.g. adapting tools or methods for different partner organisations.
Experience working with global and interdisciplinary teams to conduct and publish research.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

HR Use Only (Research G6 Clause):

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university.

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

 Lancaster University's School of Physics and Astronomy seeks to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Supernova Cosmology. The successful candidate will work with Dr Mathew Smith on an STFC-funded project to build an independent, homogeneous, low-redshift sample of SNeIa from the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), and combine it with measurements at high redshift (e.g. from the Dark Energy Survey, the Vera Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST)) to measure the equation-of-state of dark energy. 

 The work will primarily focus on two closely related areas: developing a simulation and cosmological inference framework for the ZTF survey; and measuring and modelling environmental biases, including how these interact with the survey's selection effects. The output of this project will be a low-redshift anchor suitable for use by the Vera Rubin/LSST and 4MOST-TiDES surveys.

 Candidates with experience in supernova cosmology are encouraged to apply. The post is available immediately, with an anticipated start date of 1st January 2027 (a later start, up to early Spring 2027, can be accommodated). The appointment is a fixed-term contract until September 2029. 

 In addition to joining the ZTF Collaboration, the selected candidate will join the wider Observational Astrophysics group at Lancaster, a friendly and collaborative research environment. The candidate will be welcome to participate in group research activities, which cover diverse topics including transients, high-redshift galaxies, galaxy evolution, gravitational waves and citizen science projects, and will have regular opportunities to exchange ideas across these areas. 

 If you have any queries regarding this position, please contact Mathew Smith at mat.smith@lancaster.ac.uk .

 Qualifications: 

 A PhD (or near completion) in astrophysics, physics, cosmology or a related field; strong scientific programming skills (Python); research experience in supernova cosmology, statistical or systematic-uncertainty analysis, or large-scale survey science. Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

 Application Requirements:  CV, publication list, and a 2-page research statement describing past research experience and its relevance to the project's science goals.

 Deadline:  Applications received by Friday 6th November 2026, midnight UK time will receive full consideration. 

 Compensation:  Salary commensurate with a standard postdoctoral researcher role at Lancaster.

About the role

The Leicester Experimental Cancer Medicine Centre (ECMC) is part of a UK-wide network dedicated to advancing early-phase and translational cancer research. Working across the University of Leicester and University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust, the ECMC provides the infrastructure and expertise to deliver first-in-human trials and biomarker-driven studies. As a Translational Research Technician, you will play a vital role in supporting tissue collection activities for a range of clinical research studies and early-phase trials. This includes obtaining consent to research studies from patients and volunteers, collecting samples from operating theatres and clinics across Leicester hospital sites and processing of samples in accordance with Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP) standards and Standard operating procedures.

You will also contribute to maintaining laboratory facilities, monitoring equipment, and supporting training for staff and students in tissue handling and storage.

 This position requires close collaboration with clinical teams and research colleagues to ensure timely collection of clinical specimens in compliance with regulatory requirements. You will be part of a dynamic environment where flexibility is key, as sample collections may occasionally be delayed or rescheduled.

Your work will directly support the ECMC’s mission to accelerate the development of new cancer treatments and diagnostics, making a real difference to patient care.

About you

You will hold a minimum of NVQ Level 3 (such as BTEC or ONC) in a relevant subject and have experience in a technical or clinical role involving human tissue samples. A sound understanding of regulatory requirements, including Good Clinical Practice, The Human Tissue Act and health and laboratory safety standards, is essential, along with excellent attention to detail and strong organisational skills.

You will be confident working in both clinical and laboratory settings, including operating theatres, and be able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. You will demonstrate flexibility in responding to changing clinical demands and be willing to travel between hospital sites as required.

You will also possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships and communicate confidently with a wide range of stakeholders, including patients, clinical teams, researchers, and laboratory staff.

Above all, you will share our values of inclusivity, collaboration and impact, and be motivated to contribute to research that improves outcomes for cancer patients.

Experience in an NHS or clinical research environment and experience in adhering to GCLP standards would be advantageous

Additional information
Informal enquiries are welcome and can be made to Prof Karen Brown on kb20@le.ac.uk
 
 As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role will also be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Please ensure this is discussed with your line manager prior to applying. More information regarding secondments can be found here
 
The University of Leicester has been changing the world, and changing people’s lives, for 100 years. When you join us, you’ll become part of a community of Citizens of Change, which includes not only our staff and our current students but also thousands of Leicester graduates around the world.
 
As a diverse and forward-thinking employer, we embed the principles of equity, diversity and inclusion into everything we do. That includes not just our core missions of teaching and research, but also our support for staff, students and our local community through our values of Inspiring, Impactful and Inclusive.
 
We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond. We offer a competitive salary package, excellent pension scheme and a generous annual leave allowance, along with opportunities to develop your career in a supportive and collaborative environment.

KTP Associate - Digital Manufacturing Engineer for AI based Quality Inspection
Knowledge Transfer Partnerships
Location:  Off Campus
Please note, this post is fixed-term until 31/10/2028 and full-time at 37 hours per week.
Closing Date:   Friday 30 October 2026
Interview Date:   To be confirmed
Reference:  EL1284

Are you passionate about applying artificial intelligence and computer vision to solve real-world manufacturing challenges? Do you want to take cutting-edge AI technologies beyond the laboratory and deploy them within a live industrial environment? Are you excited by the opportunity to lead an innovation project at the intersection of AI, digital manufacturing, and industrial automation?

We are seeking a KTP Associate - Digital Manufacturing Engineer for AI-Based Quality Inspection for an exciting 24-month Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) between the University of Lincoln and Eminox Ltd.

Eminox is a global leader in the design and manufacture of advanced exhaust after-treatment systems for heavy-duty on-road and off-road vehicles, rail, marine and power-generation applications. This KTP brings together Eminox's industrial expertise with research expertise from the University of Lincoln's Creative Automation Lab for Industrial X-factors (CALIX) in intelligent manufacturing, industrial automation, artificial intelligence, computer vision and Industry 4.0 technologies. 

What You'll Be Doing

Based primarily at Eminox Ltd in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, you will take a leading technical role in developing and implementing an AI-enabled vision pre-inspection system for industrial manufacturing.

You will work to first capture complex, multi-modal industrial datasets to and then develop intelligent methods capable of identifying manufacturing defects and predicting downstream performance outcomes of Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) units. Combining computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, and industrial automation, you will translate advanced AI research into a robust system capable of operating within a real manufacturing environment. 

You will lead activities including developing machine-vision methods for defect detection and classification; designing and training AI models; establishing industrial data pipelines; integrating AI algorithms with manufacturing processes; and validating and optimising the resulting system under industrial operating conditions. The aim is to improve inspection accuracy and consistency while reducing unnecessary downstream processing, manufacturing costs and waste. 

This is much more than a desk-based AI role. You will work at the interface between advanced research and industrial implementation, developing prototypes, conducting system-integrated testing, and translating theoretical approaches into commercially viable solutions. 

As the KTP Associate, you will have considerable autonomy and responsibility for delivering the project, managing technical milestones, and communicating results. You will also contribute to research outputs, technical reports, publications, and conference presentations, while developing documentation and training materials that enable the new knowledge and capability to remain embedded within Eminox beyond the project. 

What We're Looking For

We are looking for an ambitious interdisciplinary engineer who wants to apply advanced digital technologies to real industrial challenges.

A strong academic foundation: A master’s degree in mechanical engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science/Data Science, or a closely related discipline is essential. A PhD in a relevant discipline is desirable. 
AI and data expertise: Experience in machine learning, computer vision and/or data analytics, with an ability to develop and evaluate intelligent models for engineering applications. 
Strong programming capability: Programming experience in Python or similar is particularly important, with MATLAB or similar environments also relevant. Experience with deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow and computer-vision tools such as OpenCV would be advantageous. 
Engineering and experimental capability: Experience of experimental work, quality-inspection techniques, and systems, and researching and developing new or improved engineering systems or methods. 
Analytical problem-solving: Strong mathematical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyse complex data and translate technical concepts into practical industrial solutions. 
Industrial and digital manufacturing experience: Familiarity with industrial datasets, manufacturing environments, process automation and control systems such as PLCs, Industry 4.0 technologies or automated quality-inspection systems would be advantageous. 
Project leadership: The ability to manage a complex project involving multiple stakeholders, organise your own work effectively and deliver against demanding KTP and business milestones. 
A collaborative and innovative mindset: You should be proactive, adaptable, and enthusiastic about R&D, with the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary academic and industrial teams. 

Why Join Us?

This KTP offers a unique opportunity to lead the development of an industrial AI system from research concept through to implementation in a live manufacturing environment.

You will benefit from:

Direct mentorship and joint supervision from experienced engineers and senior management at Eminox and academic experts from the University of Lincoln. 
Access to a dedicated KTP personal development and training budget. 
Nationally recognised management and leadership development through the Innovate UK KTP programme. 
Experience spanning AI, computer vision, digital manufacturing, industrial automation, and real-world technology deployment. 
Opportunities to produce research outputs and engage with the wider academic and industrial research community. 
The opportunity to develop project-management, leadership, and stakeholder-engagement capabilities alongside your technical expertise. 
Strong potential for continued career development within Eminox following successful completion of the KTP. 

The project provides an unusual opportunity for an ambitious engineer or AI specialist to become the technical lead for a strategically important industrial innovation project, developing expertise that bridges advanced AI research and manufacturing practice.

The role is based primarily at Eminox Ltd in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, with regular interaction with the University of Lincoln and CALIX. The Associate will work closely with both industrial and academic teams throughout the 24-month project. 

If you would like further information or an informal discussion about this exciting opportunity, please contact Dr Faiz Iqbal (fiqbal@linoln.ac.uk), School of Engineering and Physical Sciences, University of Lincoln.

Senior Research Associate in Computer Vision and 3D Reconstruction for Wildlife Conservation - (9503)

About the Faculty 

Manchester Metropolitan University is one of the UK's largest universities, with a strong commitment to interdisciplinary research addressing real-world challenges. Our newly established School of Biological and Chemical Sciences, within the Faculty of Science and Engineering, brings together expertise spanning biodiversity, zoology, ecology, physiology and the biomedical sciences. The University has growing strengths in artificial intelligence, data science and computational research, supported by its new Centre for Digital Data Research (CDDR). Together, these strengths provide an exciting environment for research at the intersection of AI, biological sciences and conservation. 

About the School 

You will join the School's Biodiversity and Environmental Resilience research group, where researchers investigate animal biology, evolution, behaviour and conservation, and develop innovative approaches to understanding and protecting the natural world. Our research combines traditional biological expertise with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, advanced 3D imaging and computational modelling. You will benefit from access to specialist research facilities, including imaging equipment in the University's new £1m Centre for Digital Modelling and Analysis for Cultural Heritage (D-MACH), and opportunities to engage with the wider Species Biology and Conservation (SBAC) research community through seminars, collaborative activities and knowledge exchange.  

About the Project  

This position is funded by the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) through Phase 1 of its Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Science (AI4ES) programme. The project, Using Camera Trap Images to Reconstruct Wildlife 3D Body Size and Condition, aims to develop innovative AI-based methods for measuring animal size, shape and body condition from standard camera-trap photographs.  

By combining monocular depth estimation with single-image 3D reconstruction, the project will develop new approaches to recovering quantitative, real-world measurements of wild animals without the need for physical handling. Working with Chester Zoo and the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, we will develop and validate these methods using advanced 3D imaging techniques, including LiDAR and photogrammetry, with the longer-term aim of supporting non-invasive wildlife health monitoring and conservation.  

The project is led by Dr Charlotte Brassey (Principal Investigator), alongside Manchester Met colleagues Dr Selvino de Kort and Dr Bradley Cain, and external collaborators Dr Peng Wang (University of Sussex), Dr Lisa Holmes (Chester Zoo) and Dr Adam van Casteren (Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology).  

About the Role & Team 

You will play a central role in the day-to-day technical development and delivery of the project, with responsibility for developing, testing and validating AI-based approaches to reconstructing animal body size and shape from camera-trap imagery. Your work will primarily involve computational research, including model development, dataset curation and quantitative analysis, alongside opportunities for practical data collection and validation at Chester Zoo.  

You will be encouraged to take ownership of your research, contribute to peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations, and help shape future research directions, including the development of a larger Phase 2 funding application. You will also become part of the wider Biodiversity and Ecosystem Resilience research community, with opportunities to participate in the Species Biology and Conservation (SBAC) seminar series and professional development activities.  

Key Responsibilities 

Benchmark and fine-tune state-of-the-art monocular depth-estimation models using camera-trap imagery. 
Develop and evaluate AI-based methods for single-image 3D reconstruction of animals, integrating metric depth information to recover body dimensions and shape in real-world units. 
Curate and manage colour, LiDAR, photogrammetry and 3D datasets. 
Develop robust, reproducible computational pipelines using Python and relevant deep-learning frameworks. 
Undertake quantitative validation, statistical analysis and evaluation of model performance, accuracy and uncertainty. 
Collaborate with project partners to undertake data collection and validation at Chester Zoo. 
Contribute to the development and release of open-source software, datasets and trained models. 
Prepare research findings for publication in peer-reviewed journals and presentation at national and international conferences. 
Contribute to project management, dissemination, stakeholder engagement and the development of follow-on funding applications, including Phase 2 of the NERC AI4ES programme. 

Key Skills & Experiences  

We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with strong computational skills and experience in computer vision, machine learning, AI-based image analysis and/or 3D reconstruction. We welcome applicants from a broad range of disciplinary backgrounds; previous experience in ecology or zoology is not required. This is an interdisciplinary project, and we recognise that relevant expertise can be developed through a variety of research backgrounds and career pathways. We therefore encourage applications from candidates who bring transferable skills and enthusiasm for the project, even if they do not meet every criterion listed below.  

Essential criteria: 

A PhD (or close to completion) in a relevant discipline, such as Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, Computational Biology, Neuroscience, Engineering or another quantitative or computational discipline. 
Strong programming skills in Python. 
Practical experience with deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or equivalent. 
Research experience developing, adapting and/or evaluating computer-vision or machine-learning models. 
Experience of quantitative analysis and rigorous evaluation of computational methods. 
Evidence of making a demonstrable, independent contribution to research projects. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively within an interdisciplinary research team. 
Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage research activities and deadlines. 
Ability to travel to Chester Zoo and undertake on-site data collection.  

To learn more about role and requirements, please read the Job Description provided below.  

If you would like to join our people and share our ambition, we would love to hear from you! 

 

Application & Assessment Process: 

To apply, please submit a CV and covering letter detailing your suitability, on the application portal. 
For informal enquiries, about this vacancy, please contact Dr Charlotte Brassey on c.brassey@mmu.ac.uk 
Please be aware that only applications including a cover letter may be considered at shortlisting stage.  
Assessment will include a competency-based interview and a practical task to be completed on the day. Further details of the task will be provided with the interview invitation. 
Interviews are expected to be held in the w/c 16 November

We believe in working together, sharing knowledge and valuing everyone's contributions. Develop your skills, further your knowledge and be part of a team who are transforming lives, every single day! 

 

Further Information

Manchester Metropolitan University fosters an inclusive culture of belonging that promotes equity and celebrates diversity. We value a diverse workforce for the innovation and diversity of thought it brings and welcome applications from local and international communities, including those from Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic backgrounds, disabled people, and LGBTQ+ individuals. 

We support a range of flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and tailored schedules, which can be discussed with your line manager. If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or in your role, please let us know so we can provide appropriate support. 

Our commitment to inclusivity includes mentoring programmes, accessibility resources, and professional development opportunities to empower and support underrepresented groups. 

Manchester Met is a Disability Confident Leader and, under this scheme, aims to offer an interview to disabled people who apply for the role and meet the essential criteria as listed in the attached Job Description for that vacancy. 

This vacancy is expected to attract a high volume of applications. Therefore, under the Disability Confident Scheme, only disabled people who apply under the scheme and best meet the essential criteria will be offered an interview.

 Postdoctoral Research Associate Position in Neuromorphic Accelerators

 Northeastern University London

 Location:  London, Devon House (St Katherines Dock)

 Term:  1.5 years, fixed term, full-time

 Reports to:  Professor Bipin Rajendran

 Benefits:  The university supports staff maintaining a good work-life balance, offering: ( i ) flexible working and parental leave opportunities; ( ii ) an employee assistance programme which provides free, confidential advice on both home and work concerns, as well as optional private medical insurance; ( iii ) season ticket loans; and ( iv ) being part of the cycle-to-work scheme.

 Start:  ASAP 

 The Role   

 Northeastern University London invites applications for a Post-doctoral Research Associate (PDRA) in Neuromorphic Accelerators to work with Professor Bipin Rajendran as part of the NeuroWare Neuromorphic Computing Hardware Semiconductor IKC. 

 The successful candidate will work on the design, implementation and validation of hardware accelerators for state-of-the-art AI models based on neuromorphic computing and In-Memory Computing (IMC) principles for applications in enterprise, IoT and Networked Systems. 

 Core duties include:

 Contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of neuromorphic and in-memory hardware accelerators for training and inference of state-of-the-art AI models.

 Develop algorithms, architectures, and hardware–software co-design methodologies for energy-efficient AI computation on neuromorphic and in-memory computing (IMC) platforms.

 Collaborate with cross-disciplinary teams spanning hardware design, AI/ML algorithms, information theory, and systems software to enable end-to-end system integration and validation.

 Publish high-quality research outcomes in leading journals and conferences in neuromorphic computing, AI hardware, and computer architecture.

 Support the supervision and mentoring of PhD and MSc students within the research group.

 Engage with industrial and academic collaborators to support joint research activities, technology transfer, and translational impact.

 Contribute to project management activities, including technical reporting, proposal development, and dissemination of research outcomes. 

 We particularly encourage applications from those belonging to groups underrepresented in UK higher education. 

 About the Institute 

 The Intelligent Networked Systems Institute (INSI) at NU London is a newly established transatlantic research hub focused on next-generation connectivity and intelligent computing and learning systems. The INSI London Hub acts as a bridge between the US and Europe, advancing interdisciplinary collaboration across continents. INSI is dedicated to addressing pressing challenges in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, quantum information, and information processing—all with the objective of creating a more efficient, connected, and secure world. 

 About the University 

 Founded in 2012, Northeastern University London (formerly known as New College of the Humanities) has established itself as a prestigious higher education institution based in the heart of London. Northeastern University London is part of Northeastern University’s Global Campus Network. Positioned as top ranking in the USA, Northeastern has campuses in Arlington, Boston, Charlotte, Miami, Oakland, San Jose, and Seattle in the USA, and Toronto and Vancouver in Canada.

 After becoming part of Northeastern University’s global network in early 2019, the University has undergone a period of rapid growth, having been granted Taught Degree Awarding Powers in February 2020 and moved to a new, state-of-the-art campus in 2021.  

 Northeastern University London offers a vibrant, collegiate community delivering broad and academically rigorous degree programmes, designed to equip graduates with the combination of skills and knowledge that are increasingly desired by organisations, employers, and society. It offers state of the art audio visual technology in its teaching and meeting spaces across the organisation. 

 Person Specification Criteria   

 To undertake this role, the following should apply – should you not have the experience below, please do highlight where transferable skills would assist with you undertaking the role. 

 Qualifications  

 PhD in Computer Science, Electronics or Computer Engineering or related quantitative field.   

 Key Criteria   

 Strong publication record in neuromorphic hardware design demonstrated through publications in leading conferences and/or journals, with expertise extending beyond materials and device optimisation toward system- and architecture-level innovation.

 Experience in the simulation, implementation, and validation of large-scale machine learning models, including probabilistic, neuromorphic, Transformer, and/or state-space models.

 Experience with ASIC and/or FPGA design, hardware prototyping, and tapeout workflows for emerging AI hardware systems.

 Experience in hardware–software co-design approaches aimed at mitigating, exploiting, or adapting to the non-ideal effects and variability of nanoscale devices.

 Effective communication (oral and written) skills, ability to write research reports and papers in style accessible to academic audiences

 Ability to work independently and as part of a team on research programmes   

 Additional Information   

 Enquiries  

 Informal enquiries may be made to Professor Bipin Rajendran (b.rajendran@nulondon.ac.uk). However, all applications must be made in accordance with the application process specified. 

 Application Process   

 Applications should be made via the ' Apply ' button above by 23:59 on 26 October 2026. Please reference your application “ R141061 ”. 

 Applications must include a CV and covering letter of no more than one page that addresses the criteria for the role and includes names and contact information of up to three references. References will only be sought for short-listed candidates.   

 The panel will be shortlisting for this position on a rolling basis so please apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close this post before the closing date if we receive a large number of applications. 

 Participation in the equal opportunities section is encouraged, but voluntary.   

 Please note this role may require a basic or enhanced DBS check. Our organisation acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard, protect and promote the welfare of our students and staff, and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities, government guidance and complies with best practice and Ofsted requirements. You must adhere to the above if you are offered a role with NU London. 

 Applications are welcome from all sections of the community and will be judged on merit alone. We welcome applications from underrepresented groups. Candidates must be able to demonstrate their eligibility to work in the UK in accordance with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006. 

 Job sponsorship . Visa sponsorship may be available for a successful candidate for this position.

Postdoctoral Research Fellow (Principal Investigator: Prof Xiaolan Zheng)

Area
Opportunities at the University of Nottingham in Ningbo China

Location
Ningbo

Salary
Salary will be RMB 272,606 per annum, pro-rata for part-time/short-term contract.

Fixed-term

Closing Date
Saturday 14 November 2026

Reference
184719

Nottingham University Business School China Prof. Xiaolan Zheng’s research team is seeking an outstanding Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the postdoctoral research station in business administration for the development of University of Nottingham Ningbo China research agenda.

Your Responsibility

Your key responsibilities include:

To formulate and articulate research objectives, alongside developing proposals for both individual and collaborative projects, utilizing established methodologies and techniques to execute research effectively within the specified area;
To analyze data meticulously, interpret findings, evaluate scholarly texts, and contribute innovative insights, while adhering to project deadlines and collaborating seamlessly with team members and partners;
To write up research work for publication and/or contribute to the dissemination at national/international conferences, resulting in successful research outputs;
To identify opportunities and assist in writing bids for research grant applications;
To build relationships with both internal and external contacts in order to exchange information, to form relationships for future collaborations and identify potential sources of funds and/or opportunities for collaboration.

About You

The candidate must have obtained a PhD in Finance or Accounting within the past three years.
Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate with clarity on complex information. Excellent communication skills in Chinese is a plus.
High analytical ability to analyse and illuminate data, interprets reports, evaluate and criticise texts and bring new insights.
Ability to creatively apply relevant research approaches, models, techniques and methods.
Ability to assess and organise resource requirements and deploy effectively.
Ability to build relationships and collaborate with others, both internally and externally.
Some practical experience of applying the specialist skills and approaches and techniques required for the role.

About Us

Join a unique British University in China. Join a unique British University in China. University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) was the first Sino-foreign university to open its doors in China. Located in Ningbo, this award winning campus offering a UK-style education has grown to establish a student body of over 10,000 in just 21 years.

About Postdoctoral research station in Business Administration. Postdoctoral research station in Business Administration was approved to establish in Nov 2023. It is UNNC’s first postdoctoral research station, and its founding deeply aligns with the national strategic needs in promoting talent cultivation and innovation as well as that of UNNC. UNNC’s undergraduate programme of Business Administration was launched in 2004 and the doctoral programme in 2009. The subject has been listed among the world’s top academic subjects by Shanghai Ranking for four consecutive years. The discipline of Business Administration has also established teaching and research platforms at multiple levels and carried out in-depth industry university research cooperation with world renowned enterprises such as Microsoft and Amazon. In the future, UNNC will incorporate the development of the postdoctoral research station into the agenda of the university to provide talent support in efforts to promote scientific and technological innovation as well as economic and social development.

About the Research Team. Dr. Xiaolan Zheng is a professor of finance at the Nottingham University Business School (NUBS) China. She holds the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation. Her research focuses on capital structure, debt structure, dividend policy, trade credit, corporate governance, banking, digital innovation, international finance, and the influence of institutions on financial decisions. She has published in the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, Review of Finance, Journal of International Business Studies, Journal of Corporate Finance, Research Policy, and Journal of Banking and Finance, among others.

Dr. Huimin Song is a Professor of Practice in Accounting and Director of the Nottingham Global Case Center (NGCC) at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China. She also serves as an expert advisor to its Sustainable Finance Expert Group for the United Nations Global Compact. With more than 20 years of industry experience, Dr. Song brings a unique combination of international and domestic expertise. She worked for 7.5 years in investment banking and accounting firms overseas, followed by 12 years of hands-on experience in financial management and cross-border mergers and acquisitions in China. Dr. Song led the development of the case series Geely’s Acquisition of Proton, which was simultaneously selected for inclusion in three top-tier global case publications—Harvard, Ivey, and CEIBS. She also served as chief editor of the “Twenty Best in Twenty Years” Corporate Sustainability Case Collection, published globally by the United Nations Global Compact.

Dr. Zhangfan Cao is an Associate Professor of Accounting at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC). His research focuses on areas such as market-based accounting research, corporate finance and governance, supply chain finance, ESG, and the capital market. His work has appeared in leading journals, including Journal of Corporate Finance, Journal of Banking and Finance, Financial Management, British Journal of Management, Regional Studies, and International Business Review, among others.

About the Project. This project investigates the integration of non-financial factors into core corporate decision-making processes through three primary research objectives. First, this project examines how firms integrate non-financial factors into core corporate decision-making processes. It focuses on the internalization of environmental and social considerations, exploring how these forces shape resource allocation, risk management, and strategic priorities within organizations in an increasingly digitalized environment. Second, the project aims to employ rigorous empirical methods to uncover the causal mechanisms through which non-financial dimensions interact with and reshape traditional business models. By emphasizing the internal dynamics of corporate adaptation, the project examines how organizations strategically respond to evolving institutional pressures and stakeholder expectations. Third, the project seeks to generate novel insights into the real economic implications of sustainability. It contributes to a deeper understanding of modern corporate behavior by revealing how firms navigate complex trade-offs in a globalized landscape, offering a nuanced perspective on the intersection of ethics and economics.

Approximately two-thirds of this postdoctoral position's responsibilities center on developing teaching cases in sustainable finance. The successful candidate will contribute to both educational resources and scholarly publications that examine innovation and organizational dynamics within the field.

About the NGCC. The postdoctoral researcher will be based at the Nottingham Global Case Centre (NGCC). As the only center within the University of Nottingham’s three-campus system (UK, Malaysia, and China) dedicated exclusively to teaching case development, NGCC plays a pivotal role in advancing experiential learning across the university.

Operated by the School of Business at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China, NGCC has held the status of a university-level case center since its establishment. The center is committed to enhancing the quality of education across the University of Nottingham by systematically developing and integrating high-impact teaching cases that reflect cutting-edge trends and emerging challenges in global business practice. Through these efforts, NGCC continuously fosters an innovative ecosystem for case-based teaching and research.

Your Remuneration, Benefits and Support

You will be offered a fixed term contract with University of Nottingham Ningbo China for 2 years. You will be offered a minimum annual salary package of RMB272,606 with competitive benefits package. Postdoctoral Research Fellow is also able to apply RMB50,000 research funding after they start their research.  

How to Apply

Applicants should submit an application via our on-line application system before Oct 12, 2026. Only on-line applications will be accepted. Referees will be contacted prior to interview and interviews will take place in Ningbo China.

Applications should include but are not limited to the following:

A cover letter
An up-to-update CV includes academic and research achievement list
A Research proposal (Please refer to the section on project summary)

Enquiries

Informal enquiries regarding the research project may be addressed to Dr. Zhangfan Cao (Zhangfan.Cao@nottingham.edu.cn ). If you are unable to apply on-line please contact the Human Resources Office, Tel: 86 574 88180000(Ext. 6548). 

Equality and Diversity

University of Nottingham Ningbo China is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a fair, equitable and mutually supportive learning and working environment for our students and staff. It is our intention to ensure that job applicants and staff are treated solely on the basis of their merits, abilities and potential, regardless of gender, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, age, socio-economic background, disability, religious or political beliefs, trade union membership, family circumstances, sexual orientation or other irrelevant distinction.

About the Role  

About the Role

This role supports a multidisciplinary research programme focused on healthcare waste management, sustainability and decarbonisation within the NHS. Working under the supervision of Dr Xiangyu Michael Jie, the successful candidate will assist data collection and research activities across the project consortium, undertake research on NHS waste-management practices, policy development and implementation, and investigate opportunities to reduce waste-related carbon emissions.

The role will include data management and analysis, literature and policy review, stakeholder engagement, and supporting the development of evidence-based recommendations to improve resource efficiency, circularity and progress towards NHS net-zero and decarbonisation goals.

 

About You

You will have a relevant degree and experience in policy research, health systems, sustainability, healthcare waste management or a related field. Experience of analysing policy and supporting its implementation is particularly important, together with the ability to engage effectively with NHS organisations, healthcare professionals and other project stakeholders.

A strong understanding of the NHS healthcare system, its sustainability priorities, waste-management practices and net-zero/decarbonisation goals would be highly desirable. You should also be comfortable working with quantitative and/or qualitative data, coordinating activities across multidisciplinary teams, and translating research evidence into practical recommendations that can support policy and operational change.

 

About the School

The School of Physical and Chemical Sciences (SPCS) at Queen Mary University of London is a large, multidisciplinary and research-intensive school within the Faculty of Science and Engineering.

The School has a diverse and active community, with over 900 undergraduate students, more than 100 postgraduate taught students, around 115 postgraduate researchers, and approximately 150 academic and professional staff. It fosters a highly collaborative culture, working across faculties and with industry partners and external stakeholders.

SPCS is primarily based at the Mile End campus, with facilities in the G.O. Jones and J. Priestley buildings that include advanced laboratories, workshops, and shared study and social spaces. Teaching is also delivered at the London City Institute of Technology and internationally in partnership with Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT) in Hainan, China.

About Queen Mary

At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

Benefits

We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities.

Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly.

About the Role

We are seeking a Research Technician to support an industry-funded research programme on microwave-catalytic conversion of waste plastics into valuable C9+ chemicals. You will have relevant knowledge and practical experience in plastic upcycling technologies, including heterogeneous catalysis, thermochemical conversion, gas-phase reaction testing and the conversion of plastic waste into C3+ chemicals.  Queen's University Belfast 

 - School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science 

 Location: 

 Belfast

 Salary: 

 £36,366 to £41,727
 per annum (to be pro-rated for 0.6 FTE)

 Hours: 
 Part Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 19th October 2026 

 Closes: 
 26th November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 26/113701 

 About the Role 

 The post-holder will contribute to an Invest NI Proof of Concept project focused on the development of advanced antenna and RF interconnect technologies for sub-terahertz applications.

 The project aims to develop compact, high-performance antenna and interconnect solutions for next-generation high-frequency sensing and radar systems. The Research Assistant will work closely with the project team on electromagnetic design, simulation, optimisation, fabrication and experimental characterisation of antennas and RF interconnect struc tures operating at D-band frequencies.

 The role provides an opportunity to gain practical experience in advanced antenna design, high-frequency measurements and technology development leading towards an industrial demonstrator.

 About the Person 

 The successful candidate must have and your application should clearly demonstrate that you meet the following essential criteria: 

 2:1 or above BSc Honours degree (or equivalent) in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, RF Engineering, Microwave Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering or a closely related discipline.

 Specific, relevant experience of conducting engineering analysis and interpreting simulation or experimental results.

 Practical experience using at least one full-wave electromagnetic simulation package, such as CST Microwave Studio, Ansys HFSS or an equivalent tool.

 To be successful at shortlisting stage, please ensure you clearly evidence in your application how you meet the essential and, where applicable, desirable criteria listed in the Candidate Information. 

 This is a fixed-term contract for 12 months or until 31 December 2027, whichever is soonest. Fixed term contract posts are available for the stated period in the first instance but in particular circumstances may be renewed or made permanent subject to availability of funding.

 To view more information and/or to make an application, please visit our website.

Postdoctoral Research Associate

 University of Reading 

 - Philosophy, School of Philosophy Politics & Economics 

 Location: 

 Reading

 Salary: 

 £37,369 to £40,704
 per annum

 Hours: 
 Full Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 16th October 2026 

 Closes: 
 20th November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 SRF54208 

 Job description 

 This role is full time, fixed term for 12 months.

 Closing date: 23:59 on 20th November 2026

 Interview date: 10th December 2026, the interview will include a presentation element.

 Due to the complexity of the Skilled Worker Visa route and eligibility criteria, applicants requiring sponsorship are recommended to check their eligibility on the Home Office website. We cannot provide advice to candidates at the application stage and will only discuss visa routes with candidates who are invited to interview.

 There may be costs associated with a visa application, including the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS), which are not paid for by the University of Reading and cannot be claimed back. For further information on potential costs please visit:  Healthcare Surcharge Information GOV.UK. 

 The Department of Philosophy is looking for a Post-Doctoral Research Associate to join the AHRC Catalyst project Large Language Models as Philosophical Inquiry , led by Dr Jumbly Grindrod. The project works across philosophy and computational linguistics, using analyses of how large language models handle various linguistic phenomena to shed light on the nature of those phenomena themselves. Further detail on the project, including the research it builds on, is available at https://jumblygrindrod.github.io/ahrc-project.html 

 You will design and carry out the model-analysis studies at the centre of that work, collaborating closely with the Principal Investigator. You will publish and present the findings, support the organization of the project conference, as well as a special issue of the journal Ratio. 

 The post is an opportunity to gain experience in interdisciplinary research: to use interpretability methods developed in computational linguistics to pursue questions in philosophy and linguistics, and to develop expertise in an area where the two are only beginning to meet.

 You will have:

 a doctoral degree, awarded or with thesis submitted by the start date, in natural language processing, computational linguistics, machine learning or a cognate discipline;

 experience of analysing the internal representations or computational behaviour of large language models, using methods such as probing, representational analysis, or feature- and circuit-level interpretability techniques;

 experience of designing empirical studies and applying appropriate statistical methods to their analysis;

 strong programming skills in Python and experience with standard machine learning and natural language processing libraries;

 a record of producing peer-reviewed publications in reputable journals or well-respected conference proceedings.

 Familiarity with philosophy of language is desirable but not essential. We welcome applications from researchers whose background is in linguistics, cognitive science, digital humanities or related fields.

 Informal enquiries: Dr Jumbly Grindrod, Principal Investigator, j.grindrod@reading.ac.uk 

 We welcome applications from both external and internal candidates. As part of the University's ongoing commitment to professional development, this role can be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Internal candidates should discuss this with their line manager prior to applying.

 The University is committed to having a diverse and inclusive workforce, supports the gender equality Athena SWAN Charter and the Race Equality Charter, and champions LGBT+ equality. We are a Disability Confident Employer (Level 2). Applications for job-share, part-time and flexible working arrangements are welcomed and will be considered in line with business needs.

Research Assistant

 University of Salford 

 - Faculty of Science, Engineering and Environment 

 Location: 

 Salford

 £34,630 to £38,448

 Hours: 
 Full Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 22nd October 2026 

 Closes: 
 1st November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 1114-491858053 

 Opportunity Overview
 PLAN-B (the Path Towards Addressing Adverse Impacts Of Light And Noise Pollution On Terrestrial Biodiversity And Ecosystems) is an EC project involving 11 project partners from across Europe, collaborators in Brazil and a large network of international stakeholders. This research assistant role will contribute PLAN-B research on understanding the mechanisms of light and noise pollution impact on terrestrial biodiversity and ecosystem services. The role requires an individual with demonstrable expertise in the development of computer vision techniques for wildlife research and in the development of pollution impact assessment approaches/guidance to support regulatory decision-making.

 Applicants should be aware that this advert may close early if we receive a high volume of applications. 

 Key Responsibilities 

 Developing impact assessment models and guidance documents to support regulatory decision-making for light and noise pollution impacts on wildlife.

 Developing computer vision methods for analysing organism activity in field and laboratory studies.

 Planning and coordination and delivery of community and stakeholder engagement activities, including participant recruitment, workshop facilitation, and communication with external stakeholders.

 Structured literature review and database development on light and noise pollution impacts on wildlife.

 Collection, management and analysis of research data generated through research activities.

 About the Faculty of Science Engineering and Environment
 The Faculty of Science, Engineering and Environment (SEE) is a centre of discovery and innovation. Our Research and Innovation Centres work together to collaborate around the world’s greatest challenges including Net Zero, Climate Change and Resilience, Healthy Living and Industry. Our focus is on translating our pioneering research into real-world impact for people and industry and our research is recognised as world leading.

 With the largest group of research centres at the University, plus world-class test facilities such as Energy House 2.0, North of England Robotics Innovation Centre (NERIC), and the Acoustics Research Centre, we are at the forefront of pioneering discovery, nurturing the next generation of industry leaders.

 What's in it for you? 

 Competitive salary  - and excellent pension scheme.

 An impressive 32 days leave  - plus bank holidays, additional time off at Christmas and the opportunity to buy even more!

 Flexible working  - we support a culture of flexible and agile working to help you find the right balance.

 Our community  - there's a real sense of belonging here at Salford. We value diversity, in backgrounds and in experiences. Our difference makes us stronger, and together we share a passion for improving students' lives.

 The Perks!  - MySalford, our online employee portal offers a wide range of lifestyle benefits and discounts.

 Wellbeing support  - all our people are important to us and we have services and facilities dedicated to your mental and physical health, ranging from an Employee Assistance Programme and counselling to sports and fitness facilities including discounted gym memberships.

 Networking  – opportunity to develop international research networks and undertake international travel.

Research Fellow in III-V Epitaxy for Optoelectronics

 University of Southampton 

 - Photonic Systems Circuits & Sensors Group 

 Location: 

 Southampton

 Salary: 

 £36,636 to £44,746
 Per annum

 Hours: 
 Full Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 6th October 2026 

 Closes: 
 2nd November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 3520126BA 

 Location:  Highfield Campus

 Term: Full Time, Fixed Term until 31/05/2028

 Interview Date:  To be confirmed

 We are seeking a highly motivated Research Fellow with expertise in semiconductor epitaxy to join the Optoelectronics Research Centre (ORC) at the University of Southampton, one of the world's leading centres for photonics research.

 The successful candidate will join a multidisciplinary team developing advanced III-V semiconductor materials and integrated optoelectronic devices on silicon. The research programme focuses on the development of innovative epitaxial growth technologies for the integration of III-V materials on silicon and other lattice-mismatched platforms, enabling next-generation photonic devices for optical communications, sensing and emerging quantum technologies.

 The role will involve the growth and optimisation of III-V semiconductor materials using Metalorganic Vapour Phase Epitaxy (MOVPE), together with the optical, electrical and structural characterisation of materials and devices. The successful candidate will also contribute to device fabrication and integration activities within Southampton's internationally renowned silicon photonics and nanofabrication facilities.

 During the initial phase of the project, the postholder will work closely with external epitaxy facilities and project partners to undertake growth campaigns and advance the research programme while new III-V epitaxy infrastructure is established at Southampton. The role will therefore involve travel to partner organisations and requires the ability to work independently, and confidence in collaborating effectively with academic and industrial partners.

 You should hold a PhD (or near completion) in Electronic Engineering, Photonics, Physics, or a closely related discipline. Hands-on experience in the epitaxial growth of III-V semiconductors, including III-As/P/Sb and/or III-nitride materials using metal-organic vapour phase epitaxy (MOVPE) or molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), is essential. Experience in semiconductor device fabrication, cleanroom processing, and optical or electrical characterisation techniques is highly desirable.

 The successful candidate will have a strong publication record relative to career stage, excellent communication skills, and the ability to contribute effectively to a collaborative research environment spanning multiple institutions and industrial partners. You will be expected to disseminate research findings through high-quality publications and conference presentations, while helping to develop new research directions and collaborative opportunities.

Post-Doctoral Research Fellow in Climate - and Macroeconometrics - AR3355CM

 University of St Andrews 

 - Business School (Economics) 

 Location: 

 St Andrews

 Salary: 

 £38,784
 per annum Grade 6

 Hours: 
 Full Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 16th October 2026 

 Closes: 
 15th December 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 475772 

 Start Date: 1 March 2027

 Duration: Fixed Term until 31 December 2031

 We invite applications for a Post-doctoral Research Fellow to work with Dr Martin Bruns on a project Short-run Climate Change Effects: Evidence from Structural Vector Autoregression funded by the Leverhulme Trust. The project examines the economic effects of climate-related shocks such as natural disasters or weather extremes, at a monthly or quarterly frequency. To do so, a series of both methodological time series econometrics studies and applied climate-related studies will be conducted, partly in cooperation with the University of East Anglia Climatic Research Unit (CRU), the European Central Bank (ECB), and the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin).  

 The primary duties will be

 to construct a database of monthly climate shocks which can be readily used in a structural vector autoregression

 to implement novel time series econometrics methods in software packages such as R, Matlab, and Python

 to liaise with external partners such as the CRU, ECB, and DIW Berlin

 to engage in the wider research activities as part of the macro cluster at the department of economics at St Andrews Business School

 to disseminate the project findings at international conferences and related events

 to attend both internal and external training events as well as professional development opportunities

 Applications are invited for a 2-year Postdoctoral Research Associate position to work with Dr. Amit Kumar at the School of Chemistry, University of St. Andrews, on the topics of organometallic chemistry, homogeneous catalysis, and polymer chemistry.  You will have a Ph.D. in chemistry with a proven track record in homogeneous catalysis, organic, and organometallic chemistry. Effective written and verbal communication skills, good time-management and the ability to work independently, yet within a collaborative environment, are essential.

postings.advert_text:
Academic Clinical Fellow in General Practice and Data Science ST1-ST3 (Fixed Term)
Location
Brighton, UK
Hours
Full time considered up to a maximum of 1.0 FTE.
Salary
ST1 - ST3
Contract Type
Fixed Term Contract
While this role will work with Brighton and Sussex Medical School, the substantive contract will be held by the NHS and as such all applicants must apply via Oriel. Any applications received here are not able to be considered.

About the role

For this ACF we are seeking an enthusiastic candidate interested in the analysis of routinely collected primary and secondary care data. They will be training (or applying to train) in general practice and will undertake academic training alongside this, particularly in their last 2 years of training. They will receive supervision from academics in both General Practice and Data Science. ACFs in GP have a four year training programme meaning that they spend 25% of their time in ST3 & 4 undertaking research. This post has entry points at ST1,2 and 3. 

This program will utilise linked NHS hospital and primary care data to investigate the clinical consequences of medication changes initiated during hospital admissions. The successful ACF will develop a program of work exploring the critical transition point of hospital discharge to community care where there are medication changes initiated during a hospital admission (including new prescriptions, dose adjustments, and discontinuations). These medication changes have significant implications for post-discharge outcomes, which then need to be managed in primary care. A cohort of patients vulnerable to such harms will be chosen such as those with a) polypharmacy (≥5 medications prescribed), b) Multiple Long-Term Conditions (≥2 long term conditions), or c) trans people (chosen due to evidence that they may be less likely to interact with standard primary care).

Further Key Information 

Interested candidates are advised to contact Dr Liz Ford (Informatics) E.M.Ford@bsms.ac.uk, Prof Richard McManus (GP) deansoffice@bsms.ac.uk and Prof Dunx Shrewsbury (GP) d.shrewsbury@bsms.ac.uk for an early discussion.

 About the Role 

The School of Law seeks to appoint a Research Coordinator to provide administrative support for the research activities of the School of Law, particularly assisting the Research Manager and Director of Research. The successful candidate will be an integral member of the research support team and the wider professional services team, working closely with other professional staff and academic colleagues.

This is a part-time role, and applications are welcomed from candidates interested in a part-time role of 50% to 60% (18.25 to 21.9 hours per week). We offer a supportive working environment, including flexibility over days and hours of work and hybrid working. This role could be undertaken as 50%-60% FTE throughout the year, or concentrated as a higher FTE to work in school term-times only. Applicants should specify in their cover letter what FTE and working pattern they are seeking, and all applicants will be given equal consideration.

Please note that the Terms and Conditions of Employment specify that staff must live within a reasonable travelling distance of their place of work to fulfil the duties of the role.

Informal inquiries regarding this position can be made to Jennifer Paterson, Research Manager, at j.c.wilson@warwick.ac.uk . 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description  

 About You 

The successful candidate will possess experience of administrative policies and processes, will take pride in providing high quality support, and will be a positive and professional individual who enjoys interacting with a wide variety of people in an exciting and diverse university environment.

 About the Department 

The School of Law was founded in 1968, and now with over 1200 students, 70+ full-time academics and 24 professional services staff, we have evolved into a leading UK law school, being ranked in the top 10 (Times Good University Guide 2024, Guardian University Guide 2024). Our teaching quality has been recognised with National Teaching Fellowships and Warwick Awards for Teaching Excellence. Our research culture is vibrant, and our research quality has received high REF ratings (ranked 8th overall in 2021).

The dedicated Professional Services team supports the School in multiple areas of expertise including student services, student engagement and experience, research, academic technology, outreach, human resources, marketing and communications, finance, events delivery, and governance.

CommunityDiversity is one of our great strengths, and our talented staff come from many different countries and backgrounds, and we are committed to imbedding equality, diversity, and inclusion into all of our practices. Our student body is also highly diverse, with international students comprising 32% of our undergraduates and 80% of our postgraduates. In 2025, 28% of our home first-year undergraduates arrived with a contextual offer and 63% of first years identified as BAME. We are proud to be a leading department in the University in this area.

Our Athena Swan Departmental Silver Award (and University of Warwick Silver Award) recognises the advancement of gender equality, representation, progression, and success for all in academia, and we are fully committed in the Law School to endorsing the principles of Athena Swan to support staff achieve their potential. We are supportive of staff with caring responsibilities, have generous carer's, maternity, paternity, adoption and parental leave policies, onsite childcare facilities, a childcare vouchers scheme. We encourage a supportive and flexible working environment, with commitment from all levels of the organisation in promoting gender equity.
